question: How do I set up a payment plan for spring semester tuition? and is there a fee to enroll in it

body.answer:
Student Accounts offers four- and five-month plans for Spring 2027. To enroll, “Log into RCNJ Experience (Web Self-Service),” “Locate the Student Account Info card,” “Click on Bill & Payment Suite,” then “Click on the Payment Plans tab at the top of the screen or the ‘Enroll in…’” [1] The page’s last step is cut off there. The five-month plan’s down payment is available November 16–December 4, 2026; installments are due January 15, February 15, March 15 and April 15, 2027. The four-month plan’s down payment is available November 16, 2026–February 14, 2027; installments are due February 15, March 15 and April 15, 2027. [1]
Pay the down payment and non-refundable $60 set-up fee when you enroll. You must enroll and make your first installment before the semester payment deadline. [1, 2] Past-due balances of $500 or more from previous semesters must be paid before you’re eligible; late enrollment may result in a $200 late fee and/or course deregistration. [1]

**Student Accounts**: Phone: (201) 684-7495. Email: studentaccts@ramapo.edu. Location: D-Wing, First Floor. [21]

Sources: [1](https://www.ramapo.edu/student-accounts/options-policies/) [2](https://www.ramapo.edu/student-accounts/faq/) [21](https://www.ramapo.edu/campus-directory/)

question: whats the deadline to file the FAFSA for next year and what does ramapo need from me besides that

body.answer:
Financial Aid says for the 2027–2028 FAFSA, returning students should apply by April 1; new students should apply no later than May 1. Ramapo’s FAFSA code is 009344. [14]

Ramapo says no other forms are required. [23] First-year applicants must also be accepted to Ramapo; when completing the admissions application, provide your Social Security number. [22] If you’re a New Jersey resident seeking state aid, select the “optional feature” on the 2026–2027 FAFSA confirmation page. If you didn’t, go to www.hesaa.org 3–5 business days after submitting the FAFSA, choose “Report Additional Information for State Aid,” and create a login to provide the information online. [26] An older Financial Aid Forms page, updated July 2026, says to check RCNJ Experience for specifically required documents. [21]

question: what is the policy on withdrawing from a class after the deadline and does it affect my aid/satisfactory academic progress

body.answer:
The Fall 2026 academic calendar lists [21]:
- Friday, October 2, 2026: Session I Courses - Last Day to Withdraw ("W" Grade) (already passed)
- Friday, November 6, 2026: Full Semester Courses – Last Day to Withdraw from Courses (“W” Grade) (already passed)
- Tuesday, November 24, 2026: Session II Courses - Last Day to Withdraw from Courses ("W" Grade)

The Registrar’s page says a student may NOT withdraw after the published deadline. [12] The catalog says dropping or withdrawing may affect financial aid eligibility and satisfactory progress toward graduation. [8]

For extraordinary circumstances, you may seek a late administrative withdrawal. Explain why you could not follow standard withdrawal procedures (or why you did not request, or were not granted, incompletes) and identify the term. Apply before the semester ends if possible; otherwise explain why you did not apply earlier. A granted request typically results in W grades for all courses in that term, and ordinarily covers one term per appeal. The Provost or designee reviews the appeal and supporting documentation, may request a meeting or more information, and decides whether to accept it. The burden of proof is yours; the Provost’s Office sends the decision by email and processes paperwork if granted. [13] [9]

Financial aid: students who officially withdraw from or leave school before 60% of a semester concludes are subject to federal rules on how much Title IV aid they may keep or must return. The Financial Aid Office recommends meeting with them if considering withdrawing from any classes to discuss possible effects on your aid package. [1]

For satisfactory academic progress (SAP), aid eligibility is reviewed annually after spring. The listed standards include completing at least 67% of attempted credits, a 2.0 cumulative GPA for undergraduates or 3.0 for graduate students, and staying within the 150% maximum time frame. Students who fail SAP are no longer eligible for financial aid, though certain alternative loans may be available. [2]

- **Registrar**: Phone: (201) 684-7695. Email: reg@ramapo.edu. Office: D-224. [22]
- **Financial Aid**: Phone: (201) 684-7549. Email: finaid@ramapo.edu. Office: E-210. [22]

Sources: [1](https://www.ramapo.edu/finaid/faqs/) [2](https://www.ramapo.edu/finaid/policies/) [8](https://catalog.ramapo.edu/pages/R532kjMfIcfnIkM0srb3#dropping-or-withdrawing-from-a-course1) [9](https://catalog.ramapo.edu/pages/R532kjMfIcfnIkM0srb3#withdrawal-or-leave-of-absence-from-the-college) [12](https://www.ramapo.edu/registrar/withdrawing-leave-of-absence/) [13](https://www.ramapo.edu/registrar/withdrawing-leave-of-absence/) [21](https://www.ramapo.edu/academic-calendars/) [22](https://www.ramapo.edu/campus-directory/)

question: is my 1098-T available yet? need it for taxes and cant find where to get it. also how do i get a copy of last years

body.answer:
I can't see your personal records, like your grades, balance, schedule or financial aid status.

Student Accounts says Form 1098-T is provided each year on or before January 31, for students who incurred qualified tuition and related expenses and paid corresponding payments during the current tax year. The form reports the prior tax year, January 1 through December 31—not the academic year. [21] The pages don’t say whether your form is available now or explain how to check for it electronically; I don’t have verified information about your personal form or how to request a specific prior-year copy. Contact Student Accounts about both. [21]

For a paper copy, complete the [Revocation of Electronic 1098T form](https://www.ramapo.edu/student-accounts/wp-content/uploads/sites/147/2026/02/Revocation-of-Electronic-1098T_2026.pdf) and submit it to the Office of Student Accounts. The form will be printed within 5–7 business days and mailed to the home address on file with the Registrar’s Office. [1] It must be filed annually for every year you want a paper copy. [2]

**Student Accounts**: Phone: (201) 684-7495. Email: studentaccts@ramapo.edu. Location: D-Wing, First Floor. [33]

question: im a transfer student and i commute, how do i get a parking permit and where do i park

body.answer:
**Public Safety** provides the permit registration link: [https://www.ramapo.edu/publicsafety/parking-permits/](https://www.ramapo.edu/publicsafety/parking-permits/). Follow the “Parking Permit Application Instructions” [1]. Log on to the RCNJ Parking Permits website. Enter Permit Type and click Continue; complete Contact Information, click Save/Update Person, then Continue; enter Vehicle Information and click Continue; review your request and click Continue. Print or save the Registration Filed page with your request number as verification—it is not your permit. Select the correct commuter status and “student,” not “faculty/staff.” New-student permits are available for pickup during New Student Check-In [1]. The permit fee and applicable NJ sales tax are included on the term bill; off-campus students are subject to 6.63% sales tax [18]. Commuters may register two vehicles, but only one registered vehicle may be on campus at a time [8].
An older Orientation Programs FAQ (updated July 2022) describes a different PermitStore application and temporary-permit process [2].
Commuters receive a hangtag for the rearview mirror and should park in the appropriate lot [10]. The pages don’t identify which lot is designated for your regular commuter parking. Commuters may not park overnight from 2am–6am without prior Public Safety authorization; the Pavilion and Student Center lots require pre-authorization [11].

- **Orientation Programs**: Phone: (201) 684-7441. Email: orient@ramapo.edu. Office: D-207. [21]
- **Public Safety (Non-Emergency)**: Phone: (201) 684-7432. Email: publicsafety@ramapo.edu. Office: C-102. [21]
- **Public Safety (Emergency)**: Phone: (201) 684-6666. Email: publicsafety@ramapo.edu. Office: C-102. [21]

Sources: [1](https://www.ramapo.edu/orientation/faq-2/) [2](https://www.ramapo.edu/orientation/faq/) [8](https://www.ramapo.edu/publicsafety/parking-regulations/) [10](https://www.ramapo.edu/publicsafety/how-to-apply-for-a-parking-permit/) [11](https://www.ramapo.edu/publicsafety/parking-regulations/) [18](https://www.ramapo.edu/student-accounts/parking/) [21](https://www.ramapo.edu/campus-directory/)

question: my roommate keeps having his girlfriend sleep over like 5 nights a week. is there a guest policy and who do i talk to about it

body.answer:
Roommate problems are really common, and they can be worked out. Your RA is a good first step.

Yes. Ramapo says guests may not move from host to host to stay on campus more than three (3) nights. The College assumes residents agree to let roommates register guests in a shared unit, but you can opt out by contacting your Resident Assistant to set up a roommate/suitemate/apartment contract. Roommates are responsible for raising concerns with the guest’s host; the page recommends discussing guest expectations openly. If a contract is violated, the hall/area office must receive a formal complaint before staff can act. Once a complaint is received, all residents of the unit may lose guest privileges until they develop a contract. [3]
The last night residents may host overnight guests is Monday, December 14, 2026; overnight guests are not permitted on campus after that date. Residents with an approved check-out extension may not have guests. [6]

**Housing & Residence Life**: Phone: (201) 684-7461. Email: reslife@ramapo.edu. [21]

This office can help:
**Ombuds Office**: Phone: (201) 684-7804. Email: jwoods1@ramapo.edu. [22]

Sources: [3](https://www.ramapo.edu/reslife/gtcl/) [6](https://www.ramapo.edu/reslife/fallcheckoutandwinter/) [21](https://www.ramapo.edu/campus-directory/) [22](https://www.ramapo.edu/campus-directory/)

question: how do i get a parking permit and how much does it cost

body.answer:
Public Safety says to ensure the parking fee is applied to your RCNJ student account, then visit the Parking Permits webpage [4]. Orientation Programs says to follow the “Parking Permit Application Instructions” at the RCNJ Parking Permits link [1]. Log on to that site, enter Permit Type and click Continue; complete Contact Information, click Save/Update Person, then Continue; enter Vehicle Information and Continue; review your request and Continue; then print or save the Registration Filed page with your registration request number. It verifies your application but is not your permit. Select the correct housing assignment or commuter status, and choose “student,” not “faculty/staff” [1]. The fee is charged to your term bill [8][9]. Spring-only new-student rates are $125.00, $8.29 commuter tax and $25.00 resident supplement; summer-only rates are $100.00 and $6.63 commuter tax [16]. Off-campus students pay the 6.63% tax; on-campus students are exempt [9]. There is no fall-only permit [5]. New students pick up permits at New Student Check-In; returning residents at their campus mailbox; returning commuters at the Public Safety ID Office Monday through Friday during normal operating hours, or at the Public Safety Office Main Desk after 3 pm if they email to request a different pickup time [1][4].

- **Public Safety (Non-Emergency)**: Phone: (201) 684-7432. Email: publicsafety@ramapo.edu. Office: C-102. [21]
- **Public Safety (Emergency)**: Phone: (201) 684-6666. Email: publicsafety@ramapo.edu. Office: C-102. [21]

question: is it too late to withdraw from a class this semester and what happens to my transcript if i do

body.answer:
The Fall 2026 academic calendar lists [21]:
- Friday, October 2, 2026: Session I Courses - Last Day to Withdraw ("W" Grade) (already passed)
- Friday, November 6, 2026: Full Semester Courses – Last Day to Withdraw from Courses (“W” Grade) (already passed)
- Tuesday, November 24, 2026: Session II Courses - Last Day to Withdraw from Courses ("W" Grade)

The calendar dates already listed show that it depends on your course session: the full-semester withdrawal deadline has passed, but the Session II deadline has not. A student may not withdraw after the published deadline. [21][6]

For an eligible course, the Registrar processes a withdrawal submitted using the online withdrawal form, a course withdrawal form in the Registrar’s Office, or Web Self Service. After processing, you receive a W for the course, and you and the instructor of record are notified. [1]

If extraordinary circumstances prevented you from withdrawing by the deadline, you may seek a late administrative withdrawal. Explain why you could not follow standard withdrawal procedures and provide supporting documentation; the Provost or designee decides whether to accept the appeal. Typically, granted appeals result in W grades for all courses in the term. [7][2]

**Registrar**: Phone: (201) 684-7695. Email: reg@ramapo.edu. Office: D-224. [22]

Sources: [1](https://catalog.ramapo.edu/pages/R532kjMfIcfnIkM0srb3#dropping-or-withdrawing-from-a-course1) [2](https://catalog.ramapo.edu/pages/R532kjMfIcfnIkM0srb3#withdrawal-or-leave-of-absence-from-the-college) [6](https://www.ramapo.edu/registrar/withdrawing-leave-of-absence/) [7](https://www.ramapo.edu/registrar/withdrawing-leave-of-absence/) [21](https://www.ramapo.edu/academic-calendars/) [22](https://www.ramapo.edu/campus-directory/)

question: something fell off the ceiling in my bathroom and theres a leak. who do I call at night, public safety or facilities?

body.answer:
I'm sorry you're dealing with that. You're not alone, and you can ask for help.

**Facilities Management**

Phones: (201) 684-7660; (201) 684-7670 (Receiving / Storeroom) [Source](https://www.ramapo.edu/facilities/)

Email: not listed on its pages [Source](https://www.ramapo.edu/facilities/). The Facilities Management pages publish no shared unit mailbox. The General Unit Contact block gives only Service Desk and Receiving / Storeroom phone numbers, work requests go through the Service Request Portal or the Service Desk phone, and the only addresses are eight named staff members' own \(excluded\).

Offices: P-FAC [Source](https://www.ramapo.edu/facilities/)

Hours: Monday to Friday: 7:30am-4:30pm; Saturday and Sunday: Not published. Start date: not published. End date: not published. Published note: Administrative Offices Monday - Friday, 7:30 a.m. to 4:30 p.m. [Source](https://www.ramapo.edu/facilities/)

Contact note: You can submit a request using any of the following methods: Using the TMA iService Desk: Online Service Request Portal By Telephone: 201-684-7660 For Media, ITS and Telecomm requests please visit [https://helpdesk.ramapo.edu/](https://helpdesk.ramapo.edu/) If you require immediate assistance, problems such as no power, elevator malfunctions, plumbing leaks/clogs, no heat/AC any lock related problem, or health safety concerns please call the Service Desk at extension 7660. Any emergencies that occur between 4:30 p.m. and 7:30 a.m. OR on weekends should be reported to Public Safety at extension 6666. [Source](https://www.ramapo.edu/facilities/)

Report an after-hours or weekend emergency: 1. Report emergencies occurring between 4:30 p.m. and 7:30 a.m., or on weekends, to Public Safety at extension 6666. \(page: “Any emergencies that occur between 4:30 p.m. and 7:30 a.m. OR on weekends should be reported to Public Safety at extension 6666.”\) [Source](https://www.ramapo.edu/facilities/service-guide/)

Get immediate assistance for an urgent Facilities problem: 1. For no power, elevator malfunctions, plumbing leaks or clogs, no heat or AC, lock problems, or health and safety concerns, call the Service Desk at extension 7660. \(page: “If you require immediate assistance, problems such as no power, elevator malfunctions, plumbing leaks/clogs, no heat/AC any lock related problem, or health safety concerns please call the Service Desk at extension 7660.”\) [Source](https://www.ramapo.edu/facilities/service-guide/)

**Public Safety \(Non-Emergency\)**

Phones: (201) 684-7432; (201) 684-7789 (Director of Public Safety); (201) 684-7011 (Ramapo College Public Safety TDD) [Source](https://www.ramapo.edu/publicsafety/parking-regulations/)

Email: publicsafety@ramapo.edu [Source](https://www.ramapo.edu/publicsafety/parking-regulations/)

Offices: C-102 [Source](https://www.ramapo.edu/publicsafety/parking-regulations/)

Hours: Monday to Sunday: 24 hours. Start date: not published. End date: not published. Published note: The Public Safety Department is available 24 hours a day, 7 days a week, 365 days a year. [Source](https://www.ramapo.edu/publicsafety/get-support/)

Contact note: If there is an imminent danger to a student, or to the community, contact the Public Safety Department at \(201\) 684-6666. Public Safety Contact Information: secdesk@ramapo.edu Parking Permits: parkingpermits@ramapo.edu [Source](https://www.ramapo.edu/publicsafety/parking-regulations/)

**Public Safety \(Emergency\)**

Phones: (201) 684-6666; (201) 684-7789 (Director of Public Safety); (201) 684-7011 (Ramapo College Public Safety TDD) [Source](https://www.ramapo.edu/publicsafety/)

**Public Safety \(Emergency\)**

Contact note: If there is an imminent danger to a student, or to the community, contact the Public Safety Department at \(201\) 684-6666. Public Safety Contact Information: secdesk@ramapo.edu [Source](https://www.ramapo.edu/publicsafety/)

Get an immediate response to imminent danger: 1. If a student or the community is in imminent danger, contact Public Safety at \(201\) 684-6666. \(page: “If there is an imminent danger to a student, or to the community, contact the Public Safety Department at \(201\) 684-6666.”\) [Source](https://www.ramapo.edu/publicsafety/report-an-incident/)

**Housing & Residence Life**

Contact the right office for a facilities emergency: 1. Monday–Friday, 8:00 AM–4:30 PM: call Facilities at 201-684-7660. \(page: “Mon–Fri, 8:00 AM–4:30 PM \| The Office of Facilities \([https://www.ramapo.edu/facilities/](https://www.ramapo.edu/facilities/)\) \| 201-684-7660”\) 2. After 4:30 PM and on weekends: call Public Safety at 201-684-6666. \(page: “After 4:30 PM & Weekends \| Public Safety \| 201-684-6666”\) 3. 8:00 PM–12:00 midnight: contact the RA Hall Office. \(page: “8:00 PM–12:00 Midni… [Source](https://www.ramapo.edu/reslife/gtcl/)

Get immediate help with an emergency when the hall/area office is closed: 1. Call Public Safety at 201-684-6666 for immediate emergency assistance when the office is closed. \(page: “If the office is closed and you need immediate assistance for an emergency, you may call Public Safety at 201-684-6666.”\) [Source](https://www.ramapo.edu/reslife/facilities-services/)

**Dean of Students**

Direct an emergency to 911 or Public Safety: 1. Direct emergencies to 911 or Public Safety at 201-684-6666. \(page: “Emergencies should always be directed to 911 or Public Safety at 201-684-6666.”\) [Source](https://www.ramapo.edu/student-affairs/student-communications/update-to-health-services-feb2026/)

This office can help:
**Civic and Community Engagement Center**: Phone: (201) 684-7586. Email: ccec@ramapo.edu. Office: SC-213. [1]

The form may be filled out anonymously, or the survivor may choose to include identifying information. Submissions are read and responded to during regular business hours. This form is not to be used for emergencies that require an immediate response. If there is an imminent danger to a student, or to the community, contact the Public Safety Department at (201) 684-6666.
value.page_words: REPORTING TO THE MAHWAH POLICE DEPARTMENT: The Mahwah Police Department (http://www.mahwahpd.org/)can be reached by calling (201) 529-1000 or by calling 911. If a sexual assault took place within the past 5 days the responding officer will activate the Bergen County Sexual Assault Response Team (SART). SART is a free, coordinated community response to assist a survivor in the aftermath of a recent sexual assault. It has been designed to offer a compassionate, victim-centered approach while collecting evidence that can be vital to the investigation and prosecution of the crime. SART is available 24 hours a day, 7 days a week There are three members of the SART team available to a survivor. A survivor has the option to speak with all three SART members, any combination of SART members, or speak with none of the SART members. SART members include: Forensic Nurse Examiner (FNE): A FNE is specially trained in forensic evidence collection. The FNE conducts a head to toe exam and collects evidence to assist in the prosecution of the crime. Medications to prevent Sexually Transmitted Infections and pregnancy resulting from the sexual assault are also offered to the survivor. The FNE does not treat injury; anyone needing medical attention will be seen by the attending physician in the local Emergency Department. If you have any questions or concerns regarding your request, you may call our Service Desk at extension 7660; please reference the request number generated by the system when you call. return to top Asbestos: The College Park apartments were built before 1980, and some of their construction materials contain asbestos. Buckeye, Holly, International, Mimosa, Elm, Palm, Redwood, Hickory, Science, Mulberry, and Cypress have been renovated and are asbestos-free. Materials that contain asbestos include floor tiles/mastic and joint compound in walls and ceilings. These materials present no hazard unless they are impaired or disturbed. Puncturing these materials could cause a release of asbestos fibers. Please do not insert nails, tacks, hooks or otherwise impair or disturb the materials. question: I got a credit balance on my student account after my aid posted, how do I get that money sent to me? Do I need to sign up for direct deposit or does it just get mailed?

body.answer:
Student Accounts says that unless you specify otherwise, it issues a paper check mailed to your billing/permanent address; checks cannot be mailed to campus mailboxes or picked up at the office. Direct deposit is a free option. [1]

To enroll, follow “Log into RCNJ Experience,” locate the Student Account Info card, click Bill & Payment Suite, then Electronic Refunds under My Profile Setup. Enroll in Two-Step Verification (skip if already completed): in My Profile, click Security Settings, select a passcode method, click Send Code, enter the passcode and click Verify. Then click Payment Profile, edit or create a Payment Method, and check the box in the Refund Option section to designate it as the refund account. [3] The refund is expected within one to two weeks after submitting the application, if you are eligible. [2]

Student Accounts’ pages say a Title IV aid overpayment credit balance of $1.00 or greater will be refunded; credit balances from non-Title IV aid are subject to a $5.00 threshold. [1]

question: how do i add my parent as an authorized user so they can pay my bill

body.answer:
Student Accounts says adding your parent as an Authorized User lets them make payments on your behalf. [1] To set it up: [4]
1. Log into RCNJ Experience: [https://experience.elluciancloud.com/rconj/](https://experience.elluciancloud.com/rconj/)
2. Locate the Student Account Info card.
3. Click on Bill & Payment Suite link.
4. Click on Authorized Users located on the right side of the page in the My Profile Setup section.
5. Click on the Add Authorized User tab.
6. Enter the email address of the desired authorized user, answer questions, and click the Continue button.
7. Click I Agree box then the Continue button.

If you want them only to pay and not see your bill or payment history, select the ‘No’ radio button for both “View billing statement” and “View payment history.” [3] Authorized Users do not have access to your stored payment methods or personal information, and being an Authorized User does not let Student Accounts discuss your financial records with them. To permit that discussion, submit the Registrar’s Office FERPA Waiver form: [https://www.ramapo.edu/catalog/registration-policies/?ferpa=open](https://www.ramapo.edu/catalog/registration-policies/?ferpa=open). [1][6]

body.answer:
Roommate problems are really common, and they can be worked out. Your RA is a good first step.

Housing & Residence Life says room changes are not guaranteed; requests depend on available space and other factors, and professional Residence Life staff make the final decisions. [1] Review the full process at [https://www.ramapo.edu/reslife/rcp/](https://www.ramapo.edu/reslife/rcp/) and check the Residence Life Events & Important Dates calendar to understand how a room change might affect you. [1] You must submit a Room Change Request Form during the open room-change period; requests cannot be accommodated before the semester starts once housing assignments have been made. [2] The online form is at [https://docs.google.com/forms/d/e/1FAIpQLSflQtcwyqtigPCfHGI4IOscg7Zfp10vRzMMR34xv7_MDjyb6A/viewform?usp=dialog](https://docs.google.com/forms/d/e/1FAIpQLSflQtcwyqtigPCfHGI4IOscg7Zfp10vRzMMR34xv7_MDjyb6A/viewform?usp=dialog). [5] If approved, prorated housing charges and any applicable meal-plan changes will be assessed and adjusted on your student account. Housing costs vary by building, area, and housing-unit type; review costs at [https://www.ramapo.edu/student-accounts](https://www.ramapo.edu/student-accounts). [2] If you have a current parking permit, return the old permit to the Office of Public Safety (ID room) to receive a new one. [3] Unresolved conflict is among the reasons Residence Life may reassign a student, but the college reserves the right to authorize or deny roommate changes. [4]

**Housing & Residence Life**: Phone: (201) 684-7461. Email: reslife@ramapo.edu. [21]

This office can help:
**Ombuds Office**: Phone: (201) 684-7804. Email: jwoods1@ramapo.edu. [22]

Sources: [1](https://www.ramapo.edu/reslife/gtcl/) [2](https://www.ramapo.edu/reslife/new-student-guide/) [3](https://www.ramapo.edu/reslife/rcp/) [4](https://www.ramapo.edu/reslife/gtcl/) [5](https://www.ramapo.edu/reslife/rcp/) [21](https://www.ramapo.edu/campus-directory/) [22](https://www.ramapo.edu/campus-directory/)

question: how do i get a work study job on campus? i have it in my aid package but idk where to apply

body.answer:
On-Campus Employment for Students: Register on Handshake ([https://ramapo.joinhandshake.com/](https://ramapo.joinhandshake.com/)) to view open positions. Search using the keyword “RCNJ,” then follow the application instructions on each posting and contact its listed supervisor. All available positions are posted on Handshake, and Federal Work-Study recipients receive priority for Student Assistant positions. [5] You can also search the Career Center job bank on Handshake and apply to the hiring units. [2]

If offered a position and you accept, you and your supervisor sign an employment form. Return all copies of the required paperwork—the New hire packet, W-4 Form and I-9 Form—to the Student Assistant Program Office in Room D-119. [1] For questions about Federal Work-Study, reach out to Financial Aid. [5]

question: how do i find out why my financial aid hasnt shown up yet and who do i talk to

body.answer:
Money stress is really common, and you don't have to sort it out alone.

The pages don’t verify why aid has not appeared on your individual account. For information about how aid appears, use the Student Accounts FAQ’s “Click here” link, then click “Billing and Financial Aid Terminology.” [1] Financial Aid says you will receive a College Financing Plan via email within a few weeks, and that all financial aid correspondence goes to your Ramapo College email; check it regularly. [5][7]

Contact the Office of Financial Aid. You can request an in-person appointment by email or through the chat on its website. The office says most questions can be handled by phone, Webex or email; in-person appointments are available Monday through Friday from 8:30am to 4:30pm. [8]

- **Student Accounts**: Phone: (201) 684-7495. Email: studentaccts@ramapo.edu. Location: D-Wing, First Floor. [21]
- **Financial Aid**: Phone: (201) 684-7549. Email: finaid@ramapo.edu. Office: E-210. [21]

Sources: [1](https://www.ramapo.edu/student-accounts/faq/) [5](https://www.ramapo.edu/finaid/faqs/) [7](https://www.ramapo.edu/finaid/calendar/) [8](https://www.ramapo.edu/finaid/) [21](https://www.ramapo.edu/campus-directory/)

question: How do I set up a payment plan for spring semester tuition? and is there a fee to enroll in it

body.answer:
Student Accounts offers four- and five-month plans for Spring 2027. To enroll, log into RCNJ Experience (Web Self-Service) ([https://experience.elluciancloud.com/rconj/](https://experience.elluciancloud.com/rconj/)), “Locate the Student Account Info card,” “Click on Bill & Payment Suite,” then “Click on the Payment Plans tab at the top of the screen” [1]. The page’s next step is cut off after “or the ‘Enroll in” [1].

Five-month plan: down payment available November 16–December 4, 2026; installments January 15, February 15, March 15 and April 15, 2027 [1]. Four-month plan: down payment available November 16, 2026–February 14, 2027; installments February 15, March 15 and April 15, 2027 [1]. Pay the down payment and non-refundable $60 set-up fee when enrolling. Enroll by the semester payment deadline; enrolling after the down-payment due date requires paying missed installments at enrollment. Past-due balances of $500 or greater from previous semesters must be paid before you are eligible [1]. The plans do not charge interest [2].

The newer page calls the $60 charge a non-refundable set-up fee [1]; an older Student Accounts FAQ (August 2026) calls it a $60 service fee [2].

**Student Accounts**: Phone: (201) 684-7495. Email: studentaccts@ramapo.edu. Location: D-Wing, First Floor. [21]

Sources: [1](https://www.ramapo.edu/student-accounts/options-policies/) [2](https://www.ramapo.edu/student-accounts/faq/) [21](https://www.ramapo.edu/campus-directory/)

question: whats the deadline to file the FAFSA for next year and what does ramapo need from me besides that

body.answer:
For the 2027–2028 FAFSA, new students should apply by May 1; returning students by April 1 [14]. The older Financial Aid “Federal Student Aid (FAFSA)” page, updated July 2025, says new students should apply by March 15 [12].

Use Ramapo’s FAFSA school code, 009344, and apply at [https://studentaid.gov/](https://studentaid.gov/) [1]. Financial aid is based on financial need, and Ramapo says students must complete all forms in a timely manner [1, 3]. If you are an EOF applicant, submit a completed FAFSA listing Ramapo (or, if qualified as an NJ undocumented student, the NJ Alternative Financial Aid Application) and activate your NJFAMS account; additional documents may be required depending on your status [7].

question: what is the policy on withdrawing from a class after the deadline and does it affect my aid/satisfactory academic progress

body.answer:
The Fall 2026 academic calendar lists [21]:
- Friday, October 2, 2026: Session I Courses - Last Day to Withdraw ("W" Grade) (already passed)
- Friday, November 6, 2026: Full Semester Courses – Last Day to Withdraw from Courses (“W” Grade) (already passed)
- Tuesday, November 24, 2026: Session II Courses - Last Day to Withdraw from Courses ("W" Grade)

The Registrar’s policy says a student may not withdraw after the published deadline. [12] The catalog says a course withdrawal is available only through the last day to withdraw; it may affect financial aid eligibility and satisfactory progress toward graduation. [8] For an exception after standard withdrawal procedures, you may apply for a late administrative withdrawal under extraordinary circumstances. Ordinarily, apply before the semester ends; explain why you could not follow standard procedures or request incompletes, identify the term, and provide supporting documentation. The Provost or designee reviews the appeal and decides; the Provost’s Office communicates the decision in writing by email. [9]

Financial Aid says federal aid should not be affected if you remain enrolled in at least 6 credits. NJ state aid requires full-time enrollment when fully disbursed; discuss the effect on your package with Financial Aid before withdrawing. [24] If you drop below 12 credits, an Academic Scholarship or Ramapo grant may be reduced or taken away. [5] The catalog warns a course withdrawal may affect aid. Students who officially withdraw or leave school before 60% of a semester ends are subject to federal rules on aid retained or returned. [1]

For financial-aid SAP, students must complete at least 67% of attempted credits toward graduation requirements; undergraduate GPA must be at least 2.0 and graduate GPA at least 3.0 at the annual review. [2] The pages don’t specify whether a W for one course counts as an attempted credit for that calculation. [2]

Contact the Registrar about withdrawal procedures, the Provost’s Office about a late administrative withdrawal, and Financial Aid about your aid and SAP.

- **Registrar**: Phone: (201) 684-7695. Email: reg@ramapo.edu. Office: D-224. [34]
- **Financial Aid**: Phone: (201) 684-7549. Email: finaid@ramapo.edu. Office: E-210. [34]

Sources: [1](https://www.ramapo.edu/finaid/faqs/) [2](https://www.ramapo.edu/finaid/policies/) [5](https://www.ramapo.edu/finaid/academic-merit-scholarships-terms-conditions/) [8](https://catalog.ramapo.edu/pages/R532kjMfIcfnIkM0srb3#dropping-or-withdrawing-from-a-course1) [9](https://catalog.ramapo.edu/pages/R532kjMfIcfnIkM0srb3#withdrawal-or-leave-of-absence-from-the-college) [12](https://www.ramapo.edu/registrar/withdrawing-leave-of-absence/) [21](https://www.ramapo.edu/academic-calendars/) [24](https://www.ramapo.edu/finaid/faqs/) [34](https://www.ramapo.edu/campus-directory/)

question: im a transfer student and i commute, how do i get a parking permit and where do i park

body.answer:
**Getting a permit — Orientation Programs:** Go to [RCNJ Parking Permits](https://www.ramapo.edu/publicsafety/parking-permits/) and follow the Parking Permit Application Instructions. “Log on directly” to the site; “Enter Permit Type and click Continue”; complete Contact Information, click “Save/Update Person” and “Continue”; enter Vehicle Information and click “Continue”; review your request and click “Continue”; then print or save the Registration Filed page with your request number as application verification. It is not your permit. Select the correct commuter status. New students’ permits are available for pick-up during New Student Check-In. For a different pick-up time, returning commuters can email parkingpermits@ramapo.edu. [1] The older Orientation Programs FAQ (July 2022) gives different application steps. [2]

**Parking — Public Safety:** Commuters receive a rearview-mirror hangtag and should park in the appropriate lot; the Public Safety regulations page has the lot information. [7] C1, C2 or D lots are overflow if your assigned lot is full. Commuters may not park overnight (2 a.m.–6 a.m.) without prior Public Safety authorization. [8]

- **Orientation Programs**: Phone: (201) 684-7441. Email: orient@ramapo.edu. Office: D-207. [21]
- **Public Safety (Non-Emergency)**: Phone: (201) 684-7432. Email: publicsafety@ramapo.edu. Office: C-102. [21]
- **Public Safety (Emergency)**: Phone: (201) 684-6666. Email: publicsafety@ramapo.edu. Office: C-102. [21]

Sources: [1](https://www.ramapo.edu/orientation/faq-2/) [2](https://www.ramapo.edu/orientation/faq/) [7](https://www.ramapo.edu/publicsafety/how-to-apply-for-a-parking-permit/) [8](https://www.ramapo.edu/publicsafety/parking-regulations/) [21](https://www.ramapo.edu/campus-directory/)

question: I'm a commuter student and I have a 3 hour gap between classes. Is there somewhere on campus I can study or hang out, like a commuter lounge, and is there a way to store my stuff?

body.answer:
Yes. J. Lee’s is the unofficial Commuter Lounge, on the second floor of the Student Center between the Student Government and Black Student Union offices; it has games and free popcorn. [1] The Women’s Center lounge in C-220 welcomes students to hang out, socialize, or study during open hours. [14] The Atrium in the Robert A. Scott Student Center has lounging areas designed with commuter and resident students in mind. [20]

For storage, the Center for Student Involvement says students may rent small or medium lockers by coming to the Student Center Office. The lockers are in the second-floor stairwell area between B and C buildings. The fee is $10.00 for a semester or $20.00 for the academic year; you receive a key with payment and must return it at the end of the semester. [6]

**Center for Student Involvement**: Phone: (201) 684-7593. Email: csi@ramapo.edu. Office: SC-202. [21]

Roommate problems are really common, and they can be worked out. Your RA is a good first step.

Yes. Guests may not move from host to host to stay on-campus more than three (3) nights. All residents are responsible for their guests, and the page recommends discussing guest expectations with your roommate. You can contact your Resident Assistant to facilitate a roommate/suitemate/apartment contract. If someone violates that contract, staff in the hall/area office must receive a formal complaint before they can act; after a complaint, all residents of the space may lose guest privileges until they develop a contract. Orientation Programs’ current instructions: go to [RCNJ Parking Permits](https://www.ramapo.edu/publicsafety/parking-permits/). “Enter Permit Type and click Continue.” Complete the Contact Information page, click “Save/Update Person” and “Continue”; enter Vehicle Information and click “Continue”; review your request and click “Continue”; then print or save the Registration Filed page with your request number. This is application verification, not your permit. Select the correct housing assignment or commuter status, and select “student,” not “faculty/staff.” [1]
Public Safety says the parking fee must be applied to your RCNJ student account before you visit the Parking Permits webpage. Commuters receive a hangtag for the rearview mirror. [1,8] An older Orientation Programs FAQ (July 2022) gives different application instructions. [2]
For 2026–2027, the Fall/Spring permit (valid through Spring 2027) is $250.00. The Fall/Spring commuter parking tax charge is $16.58; on-campus students are exempt from the tax. Resident students have an additional $50.00 Resident Parking Supplement. The fee and applicable tax are included on the term bill. [9,16]

question: is it too late to withdraw from a class this semester and what happens to my transcript if i do

body.answer:
The Fall 2026 academic calendar lists [21]:
- Friday, October 2, 2026: Session I Courses - Last Day to Withdraw ("W" Grade) (already passed)
- Friday, November 6, 2026: Full Semester Courses – Last Day to Withdraw from Courses (“W” Grade) (already passed)
- Tuesday, November 24, 2026: Session II Courses - Last Day to Withdraw from Courses ("W" Grade)

For a full-semester course, the withdrawal deadline has passed; a Session II course is still within its listed withdrawal window. The Registrar says a student may not withdraw after the published deadline. [6] Before the deadline, withdrawal is available through an online withdrawal form, a course withdrawal form at the Office of the Registrar, or Web Self Service. [1]

After the deadline, the Office of the Provost may consider a Late Administrative Withdrawal for extraordinary circumstances. Explain why you could not follow standard withdrawal procedures (or request an incomplete), indicate the term, and provide supporting documentation; the Provost or designee decides whether to accept the application. [2] Ordinarily, apply before the semester ends. [2]

For a processed course withdrawal, you receive a W on your transcript, and you and the instructor of record are notified. [1] A granted late administrative withdrawal typically results in W grades in all courses for the term. [2]

- **Registrar**: Phone: (201) 684-7695. Email: reg@ramapo.edu. Office: D-224. [22]
- **Office of the Provost**: Phone: (201) 684-7330. Email: provost@ramapo.edu. Location: first floor of the Birch Mansion. [22]

Sources: [1](https://catalog.ramapo.edu/pages/R532kjMfIcfnIkM0srb3#dropping-or-withdrawing-from-a-course1) [2](https://catalog.ramapo.edu/pages/R532kjMfIcfnIkM0srb3#withdrawal-or-leave-of-absence-from-the-college) [6](https://www.ramapo.edu/registrar/withdrawing-leave-of-absence/) [21](https://www.ramapo.edu/academic-calendars/) [22](https://www.ramapo.edu/campus-directory/)

question: something fell off the ceiling in my bathroom and theres a leak. who do I call at night, public safety or facilities?

body.answer:
I'm sorry you're dealing with that. You're not alone, and you can ask for help.

**Facilities Management**

Phones: (201) 684-7660; (201) 684-7670 (Receiving / Storeroom) [Source](https://www.ramapo.edu/facilities/)

Offices: P-FAC [Source](https://www.ramapo.edu/facilities/)

Contact note: You can submit a request using any of the following methods: Using the TMA iService Desk: Online Service Request Portal By Telephone: 201-684-7660 For Media, ITS and Telecomm requests please visit [https://helpdesk.ramapo.edu/](https://helpdesk.ramapo.edu/) If you require immediate assistance, problems such as no power, elevator malfunctions, plumbing leaks/clogs, no heat/AC any lock related problem, or health safety concerns please call the Service Desk at extension 7660. Any emergencies that occur between 4:30 p.m. and 7:30 a.m. OR on weekends should be reported to Public Safety at extension 6666. [Source](https://www.ramapo.edu/facilities/)

Hours: Monday to Friday: 7:30am-4:30pm; Saturday and Sunday: Not published. Start date: not published. End date: not published. Published note: Administrative Offices Monday - Friday, 7:30 a.m. to 4:30 p.m. [Source](https://www.ramapo.edu/facilities/)

Report an after-hours or weekend emergency: 1. Report emergencies occurring between 4:30 p.m. and 7:30 a.m., or on weekends, to Public Safety at extension 6666. \(page: “Any emergencies that occur between 4:30 p.m. and 7:30 a.m. OR on weekends should be reported to Public Safety at extension 6666.”\) [Source](https://www.ramapo.edu/facilities/service-guide/)

Get immediate assistance for an urgent Facilities problem: 1. For no power, elevator malfunctions, plumbing leaks or clogs, no heat or AC, lock problems, or health and safety concerns, call the Service Desk at extension 7660. \(page: “If you require immediate assistance, problems such as no power, elevator malfunctions, plumbing leaks/clogs, no heat/AC any lock related problem, or health safety concerns please call the Service Desk at extension 7660.”\) [Source](https://www.ramapo.edu/facilities/service-guide/)

**Public Safety \(Non-Emergency\)**

Phones: (201) 684-7432; (201) 684-7789 (Director of Public Safety); (201) 684-7011 (Ramapo College Public Safety TDD) [Source](https://www.ramapo.edu/publicsafety/parking-regulations/)

Offices: C-102 [Source](https://www.ramapo.edu/publicsafety/parking-regulations/)

Contact note: If there is an imminent danger to a student, or to the community, contact the Public Safety Department at \(201\) 684-6666. Public Safety Contact Information: secdesk@ramapo.edu Parking Permits: parkingpermits@ramapo.edu [Source](https://www.ramapo.edu/publicsafety/parking-regulations/)

Hours: Monday to Sunday: 24 hours. Start date: not published. End date: not published. Published note: The Public Safety Department is available 24 hours a day, 7 days a week, 365 days a year. [Source](https://www.ramapo.edu/publicsafety/get-support/)

**Public Safety \(Emergency\)**

Phones: (201) 684-6666; (201) 684-7789 (Director of Public Safety); (201) 684-7011 (Ramapo College Public Safety TDD) [Source](https://www.ramapo.edu/publicsafety/)

**Housing & Residence Life**

Contact the right office for a facilities emergency: 1. Monday–Friday, 8:00 AM–4:30 PM: call Facilities at 201-684-7660. \(page: “Mon–Fri, 8:00 AM–4:30 PM \| The Office of Facilities \([https://www.ramapo.edu/facilities/](https://www.ramapo.edu/facilities/)\) \| 201-684-7660”\) 2. After 4:30 PM and on weekends: call Public Safety at 201-684-6666. \(page: “After 4:30 PM & Weekends \| Public Safety \| 201-684-6666”\) 3. 8:00 PM–12:00 midnight: contact the RA Hall Office. \(page: “8:00 PM–12:00 Midni… [Source](https://www.ramapo.edu/reslife/gtcl/)

This office can help:
**Civic and Community Engagement Center**: Phone: (201) 684-7586. Email: ccec@ramapo.edu. Office: SC-213. [1]

Sources: [1](https://www.ramapo.edu/campus-directory/)

question: whats my current balance and do i have any holds on my account

body.answer:
I can't see your personal records, like your grades, balance, schedule or financial aid status.

I can’t see your personal balance or hold status. To check your current balance, log into RCNJ Experience (Web Self-Service) and open the Bill & Payment Suite; it provides current, real-time account activity and balances and lets you run an On-Demand Statement. [https://experience.elluciancloud.com/rconj/](https://experience.elluciancloud.com/rconj/) [24] Ramapo recommends logging in periodically because balances can change. [30]

I don’t have verified instructions for viewing all holds on your account. Student Accounts says a student with an unpaid outstanding balance will have a Hold Flag; it may also be possible to have a hold from another office or department. [3] For your financial standing or a financial hold, contact the Office of Student Accounts. [14]

**Student Accounts**: Phone: (201) 684-7495. Email: studentaccts@ramapo.edu. Location: D-Wing, First Floor. [33]

question: My RA wrote me up for a candle. what happens now? do i have to go to a hearing

body.answer:
Residence Life lists using candles as prohibited. Residence Life staff address violations, and a Residence Life staff member, Public Safety, or the College Fire Marshal may confiscate prohibited items. For questions about the item, seek guidance from your Residence/Area Director. [14]

The listed $150 fine and fire-safety reflection assignment apply to a first offense for activating a fire alarm due to disregard of policy (candles are an example); they are not stated as an automatic consequence of a candle write-up. [2] For a second offense under that same rule, the newer page lists a $300 fine, disciplinary probation, and possible suspension or loss of housing privileges. [2] An older Recommended Judicial Sanctions page (updated October 2022) describes the possible housing consequence differently: possible suspension of residence privileges. [6]

I don’t have verified information that your specific write-up requires a hearing. The hearing page gives preparation guidance, including that you may have an advisor of your choosing, who cannot speak during the hearing. [1] Contact the Office of Student Conduct to ask whether you must attend and what happens in your case.

- **Housing & Residence Life**: Phone: (201) 684-7461. Email: reslife@ramapo.edu. [21]
- **Office of Student Conduct**: Phone: (201) 684-7869. Email: studentconduct@ramapo.edu. Office: C-212. [21]

Sources: [1](https://www.ramapo.edu/student-conduct/hearing/) [2](https://www.ramapo.edu/student-conduct/fire-safety/) [6](https://www.ramapo.edu/student-conduct/recommended-judicial-sanctions/) [14](https://www.ramapo.edu/reslife/gtcl/) [21](https://www.ramapo.edu/campus-directory/)

question: I got a credit balance on my student account after my aid posted, how do I get that money sent to me? Do I need to sign up for direct deposit or does it just get mailed?

body.answer:
Student Accounts says that, unless you specify otherwise, the College issues a paper check mailed to your billing/permanent address; checks are not sent to campus mailboxes and cannot be picked up at the office. Direct deposit is a free option. [1]

To enroll, follow “Setting Up an Online Payment Profile with Refund Option”: [3]
1. Log into [RCNJ Experience](https://experience.elluciancloud.com/rconj/).
2. Locate the Student Account Info card and click on Bill & Payment Suite.
3. Click on Electronic Refunds on the right hand side of the screen under the My Profile Setup menu.
4. Enroll in Two-Step Verification (skip if previously completed): in Security Settings, select a passcode method, click Send Code, enter the passcode and click Verify.
5. In Payment Profile, edit or create a payment method and check the Refund Option box to designate it for direct deposit.

After applying, you can expect the refund in your account within one to two weeks. [2] For assistance, contact Student Accounts. [2]

**Student Accounts**: Phone: (201) 684-7495. Email: studentaccts@ramapo.edu. Location: D-Wing, First Floor. [21]

Sources: [1](https://www.ramapo.edu/student-accounts/deposits/) [2](https://www.ramapo.edu/student-accounts/direct-deposit-questions-answers/) [3](https://www.ramapo.edu/student-accounts/direct-deposit/) [21](https://www.ramapo.edu/campus-directory/)

question: how do i add my parent as an authorized user so they can pay my bill

body.answer:
Student Accounts explains that an Authorized User can make payments on your behalf. [1]

1. Log into [RCNJ Experience](https://experience.elluciancloud.com/rconj/).
2. Locate the Student Account Info card and click Bill & Payment Suite.
3. Click Authorized Users on the right side of the page in the My Profile Setup section.
4. Click Add Authorized User, enter your parent’s email address, answer the questions, and click Continue.
5. Click the I Agree box, then Continue. [4]

If you want them to make payments without seeing your eBill or payment history, select “No” for both “View billing statement” and “View payment history.” Your parent will be emailed a link, user name, and password to access the Bill and Payment Suite. [3]

Authorizing a user does not permit Student Accounts to discuss your financial records with them; the newer FAQ says to submit the Registrar’s Office FERPA Waiver form, available [here](https://www.ramapo.edu/catalog/registration-policies/?ferpa=open). [1][6] The older “Allow Others to Make a Payment and/or View Your Bill” page (updated March 2026) instead names an Office of Student Accounts FERPA Waiver Form. [1]

**Student Accounts**: Phone: (201) 684-7495. Email: studentaccts@ramapo.edu. Location: D-Wing, First Floor. [21]

body.answer:
The Registrar’s instructions for new students: visit [Ramapo email](https://password.ramapo.edu/) and click “Activate E-mail Account.” You can activate within 24 hours of receiving your Ramapo ID number. [4] When signing in, approve the prompt in the Gmail app on your phone. You may select “Trust this device” on your personal device; never trust a public or shared computer. [2][4]

ResNET requires you to register the device you’ll use before it can connect to the college network; once registered, it can be used campus-wide. You need a valid Ramapo email account. [3][6] On the registration page, choose wired or wireless, retrieve the MAC address for that connection, then follow the applicable registration link: [wireless](http://mydevices.ramapo.edu/) or [wired](https://resnet.ramapo.edu/register/login.php). [14][15] For wireless, scan for networks and connect. [17] If you’re using an iPad, select “Ramapo-Secure,” enter your Ramapo username and password, then click “Accept” at the certificate warning. question: how do i switch roommates? we're not getting along at all

body.answer:
Roommate problems are really common, and they can be worked out. Your RA is a good first step.

Housing & Residence Life handles room changes. Review the [Room Change Process](https://www.ramapo.edu/reslife/rcp/) and the [Residence Life Events & Important Dates calendar](https://www.ramapo.edu/reslife/critical-housing-dates-deadlines-calendar/) before submitting; the calendar can help you understand how a change might affect you. [1] You must submit a Room Change Request Form during an open room change period. The online form is [here](https://docs.google.com/forms/d/e/1FAIpQLSflQtcwyqtigPCfHGI4IOscg7Zfp10vRzMMR34xv7_MDjyb6A/viewform?usp=dialog); it is available during active room change periods. [2][5] Changes aren’t guaranteed; they depend on available space and other factors, and Residence Life staff make the final decision. [1] If approved, prorated housing charges and any applicable meal-plan changes will be adjusted on your student account. [2] If you have a parking permit, return your old permit to Public Safety’s ID room to receive a new one. [3] The office may reassign students for unresolved conflict, but this does not guarantee a requested change. [4]

**Housing & Residence Life**: Phone: (201) 684-7461. Email: reslife@ramapo.edu. [21]

This office can help:

question: how do i get a work study job on campus? i have it in my aid package but idk where to apply

body.answer:
On-Campus Employment for Students: Register on Handshake to view open positions, then search using the keyword “RCNJ.” Apply through the instructions on each posting and contact its listed supervisor. All available Student Assistant positions are posted on Handshake; priority is given to students awarded Federal Work-Study. [5] The FAQ also directs students to search the Career Center job bank on Handshake and apply to the hiring units. [2]

If you accept a job offer, you and your supervisor sign an employment form. Return all copies of the required paperwork—the New hire packet, W-4 Form and I-9 Form—to the Student Assistant Program Office, Room D-119. [1]

For questions about your Federal Work-Study award, contact Financial Aid. [5]

**On-Campus Employment for Students**: Phone: (201) 684-7654. Email: sap@ramapo.edu. Office: D-119. [21]

Sources: [1](https://www.ramapo.edu/on-campus-employment/policies-and-procedures/) [2](https://www.ramapo.edu/on-campus-employment/faqs/) [5](https://www.ramapo.edu/on-campus-employment/) [21](https://www.ramapo.edu/campus-directory/)

question: how do i find out why my financial aid hasnt shown up yet and who do i talk to

body.answer:
I can't see your personal records, like your grades, balance, schedule or financial aid status. Money stress is really common, and you don't have to sort it out alone.

To check your account, follow “Click here” to the Billing and Financial Aid Terminology page, then click “Billing and Financial Aid Terminology.” [1] Aid shown as a Memo has not met all the requirements for payment. The page strongly recommends contacting the Office of Financial Aid to resolve outstanding issues. [2] I can’t verify the reason for your specific aid. The Office of Financial Aid is scheduling in-person appointments by email or through the chat on its website; it says most questions can be handled by phone, Webex or email. In-person appointments are Monday through Friday, 8:30am to 4:30pm. [11]

- **Student Accounts**: Phone: (201) 684-7495. Email: studentaccts@ramapo.edu. Location: D-Wing, First Floor. [21]
- **Financial Aid**: Phone: (201) 684-7549. Email: finaid@ramapo.edu. Office: E-210. [21]

question: How do I set up a payment plan for spring semester tuition? and is there a fee to enroll in it

body.answer:
Student Accounts offers four- and five-month plans for Spring 2027. To enroll, follow the page’s instructions: “Log into RCNJ Experience (Web Self-Service)” at [https://experience.elluciancloud.com/rconj/](https://experience.elluciancloud.com/rconj/); “Locate the Student Account Info card”; “Click on Bill & Payment Suite”; then “Click on the Payment Plans tab at the top of the screen or the ‘Enroll in’” option. [1]

The five-month plan’s down payment is available November 16–December 4, 2026; installments are due January 15, February 15, March 15 and April 15, 2027. The four-month plan’s down payment is available November 16, 2026–February 14, 2027; installments are due February 15, March 15 and April 15, 2027. Pay the down payment and the non-refundable $60 setup fee at enrollment. Enroll and make your first installment before the semester payment deadline. [1][2]

Past-semester balances of $500 or more must be paid before you are eligible; the College may deny enrollment based on past payment history. A $35 late fee applies to each late installment. [1]

**Student Accounts**: Phone: (201) 684-7495. Email: studentaccts@ramapo.edu. Location: D-Wing, First Floor. [21]

Sources: [1](https://www.ramapo.edu/student-accounts/options-policies/) [2](https://www.ramapo.edu/student-accounts/faq/) [21](https://www.ramapo.edu/campus-directory/)

question: refund

body.answer:
For student-account credit-balance refunds, contact Student Accounts. A Title IV financial aid overpayment that creates a credit balance of $1.00 or greater will be refunded; credit balances from non-Title IV financial aid are subject to a $5.00 threshold. Unless you specify otherwise, the College issues a paper check mailed to your billing/permanent address; checks cannot be mailed to campus mailboxes or picked up at Student Accounts. If entitled to a fall-term refund, you may ask to have it applied to the spring term by emailing studentaccts@ramapo.edu. Spring refund proceeds cannot be applied to the following fall term. [1]

Electronic refunds are free. To set one up: log into RCNJ Experience; locate the Student Account Info card; click Bill & Payment Suite; click Electronic Refunds under My Profile Setup; enroll in Two-Step Verification (skip if already completed); in My Profile, click Security Settings, select a passcode method, click Send Code, enter the passcode and click Verify; click Payment Profile; edit or create a payment method and check the box in Refund Option to designate it as the direct-deposit refund account. [6]

**Student Accounts**: Phone: (201) 684-7495. Email: studentaccts@ramapo.edu. Location: D-Wing, First Floor. [21]

Sources: [1](https://www.ramapo.edu/student-accounts/deposits/) [6](https://www.ramapo.edu/student-accounts/direct-deposit/) [21](https://www.ramapo.edu/campus-directory/)

question: whats the deadline to file the FAFSA for next year and what does ramapo need from me besides that

body.answer:
For 2027–2028, the FAFSA is open. Returning students should apply by April 1; new students by May 1. Use Ramapo’s code, 009344, at studentaid.gov. [14]

Financial Aid says no other forms are required to apply. [24] To be considered, applicants must complete the FAFSA and be accepted to Ramapo; include your Social Security number on your admissions application. If you are a New Jersey resident seeking state aid, select the “optional feature” link on the 2026-2027 FAFSA confirmation page. If you didn’t, go to hesaa.org 3–5 business days after submitting the FAFSA, select “Report Additional Information for State Aid,” and create a state-system login to provide the information online. [27]

question: what is the policy on withdrawing from a class after the deadline and does it affect my aid/satisfactory academic progress

body.answer:
The Fall 2026 academic calendar lists [21]:
- Friday, October 2, 2026: Session I Courses - Last Day to Withdraw ("W" Grade) (already passed)
- Friday, November 6, 2026: Full Semester Courses – Last Day to Withdraw from Courses (“W” Grade) (already passed)
- Tuesday, November 24, 2026: Session II Courses - Last Day to Withdraw from Courses ("W" Grade)

The Registrar’s policy says a student may not withdraw after the published deadline. Before that deadline, after the 50% refund period, you can use a withdrawal form online, complete one in the Registrar’s Office, or withdraw through Web Self Service; once processed, you receive a W and you and the instructor are notified. [8][12]

For a late exception, the Provost’s Office handles a late administrative withdrawal under extraordinary circumstances. Ordinarily, apply before semester’s end; explain why you could not use standard withdrawal procedures or request an incomplete, identify the term, and submit an appeal letter with supporting documentation. The Provost or designee decides whether to accept it; the burden of proof is yours. [13]

A course withdrawal may affect financial aid and satisfactory progress toward graduation. The Financial Aid Office recommends discussing how withdrawing from any classes may affect your current aid package. [8][1] Its SAP policy reviews progress annually after spring: students must complete at least 67% of attempted credits and meet the applicable GPA standard (2.0 undergraduate; 3.0 graduate). The policy does not specify the exact effect of one course withdrawal on your aid or SAP. [2]

For a late administrative withdrawal, contact the Provost’s Office. For aid implications, contact the Financial Aid Office.

- **Office of the Provost**: Phone: (201) 684-7330. Email: provost@ramapo.edu. Location: first floor of the Birch Mansion. [22]
- **Registrar**: Phone: (201) 684-7695. Email: reg@ramapo.edu. Office: D-224. [22]

question: im a transfer student and i commute, how do i get a parking permit and where do i park

body.answer:
For a parking permit, Public Safety says to open the [RCNJ Parking Permits](https://www.ramapo.edu/publicsafety/parking-permits/) page and follow its application instructions. [1] You can also use the [Parking Permit Registration link](https://rcnjpublicsafety.omnigo.one/CESIReportExec/opr/OPRMain.aspx?IsAuth=1&groupid=102&groupname=PUBLIC+SAFETY). [13] Enter Permit Type and click Continue; complete Contact Information, click Save/Update Person, then Continue; enter Vehicle Information and Continue; review your request and Continue; print or save the Registration Filed page with your registration request number. That page verifies your application; it is not your permit. Select the correct commuter status and “student,” not “faculty/staff.” New-student permits are available for pick-up during New Student Check-In. [1]

Public Safety says commuters receive a hangtag and should park in the appropriate lot; its page points to the [parking regulations](https://www.ramapo.edu/publicsafety/parking-regulations/). [14] The pages provided don’t identify a specific lot for commuter students. Commuters may register two vehicles, but only one registered vehicle may be parked on campus at a time. Commuters may not leave a vehicle overnight (2am – 6am) without prior authorization from Public Safety. [12][15]

- **Orientation Programs**: Phone: (201) 684-7441. Email: orient@ramapo.edu. Office: D-207. [21]
- **Public Safety (Non-Emergency)**: Phone: (201) 684-7432. Email: publicsafety@ramapo.edu. Office: C-102. [21]
- **Public Safety (Emergency)**: Phone: (201) 684-6666. Email: publicsafety@ramapo.edu. Office: C-102. [21]

Sources: [1](https://www.ramapo.edu/orientation/faq-2/) [12](https://www.ramapo.edu/publicsafety/parking-regulations/) [13](https://www.ramapo.edu/publicsafety/how-to-apply-for-a-parking-permit/) [14](https://www.ramapo.edu/publicsafety/how-to-apply-for-a-parking-permit/) [15](https://www.ramapo.edu/publicsafety/parking-regulations/) [21](https://www.ramapo.edu/campus-directory/)

question: what is the deadline to drop a class without a W and how do i do it

question: my roommate keeps having his girlfriend sleep over like 5 nights a week. is there a guest policy and who do i talk to about it

body.answer:
Roommate problems are really common, and they can be worked out. Your RA is a good first step.

Yes. The policy says guests may not move from host to host to stay on campus more than three (3) nights. Roommates may opt out of automatic guest registration by contacting their Resident Assistant to facilitate a roommate contract. If the contract is violated, hall/area office staff need a formal complaint before they can act; all residents of the space may lose guest privileges until they develop a contract. The policy recommends discussing guest expectations with your roommate. [3]
Overnight guests are permitted until Monday, December 14, 2026; they are not permitted on campus after that date. [6]
Talk to your Resident Assistant about facilitating a roommate contract. If you believe this involves a violation of the Guide to Community Living, the complaint policy directs students to Office of Residence Life. [3][16]

**Housing & Residence Life**: Phone: (201) 684-7461. Email: reslife@ramapo.edu. [21]

This office can help:
**Ombuds Office**: Phone: (201) 684-7804. Email: jwoods1@ramapo.edu. [22]

Sources: [3](https://www.ramapo.edu/reslife/gtcl/) [6](https://www.ramapo.edu/reslife/fallcheckoutandwinter/) [16](https://www.ramapo.edu/policies/policy/student-complaints-of-a-non-academic-nature/) [21](https://www.ramapo.edu/campus-directory/) [22](https://www.ramapo.edu/campus-directory/)

question: how do i get a parking permit and how much does it cost

body.answer:
Student Accounts says the 2026–2027 Fall/Spring Parking Permit is $250.00, valid through Spring 2027. Resident students also have a $50.00 supplement; off-campus students are charged 6.63% New Jersey sales tax on the parking fee. The fee is automatically included on your term bill. [9][16]

To apply, go to the [Parking Permits registration portal](https://www.ramapo.edu/publicsafety/parking-permits/). The newer instructions say to ensure the parking fee has been applied to your RCNJ student account, then visit the Parking Permits webpage. [4] You can also start by clicking “Click Here for Parking Permit Registration.” [3][6]

The Orientation Programs instructions provide these application steps: log on directly to the RCNJ Parking Permits website; enter Permit Type and click Continue; complete Contact Information and click Save/Update Person, then Continue; enter Vehicle Information and click Continue; review your request and click Continue; then print or save the Registration Filed page with your registration request number as verification. That page is not your permit. Select the correct housing assignment or commuter status, and select “student,” not “faculty/staff.” [1]

New students pick up permits during New Student Check-In. Returning resident students pick them up from their on-campus mailbox. Returning commuter students pick them up from the Public Safety ID Office Monday through Friday during normal operating hours, or from the Public Safety Office Main Desk after 3 pm if they email parkingpermits@ramapo.edu to request another pick-up time. [1][4]

The Public Safety regulations page was updated November 2026; an older Orientation Programs page (updated September 2026) gives different application and verification instructions. [4][1]

- **Student Accounts**: Phone: (201) 684-7495. Email: studentaccts@ramapo.edu. Location: D-Wing, First Floor. [21]
- **Public Safety (Non-Emergency)**: Phone: (201) 684-7432. Email: publicsafety@ramapo.edu. Office: C-102. [21]
- **Public Safety (Emergency)**: Phone: (201) 684-6666. Email: publicsafety@ramapo.edu. Office: C-102. [21]

Sources: [1](https://www.ramapo.edu/orientation/faq-2/) [3](https://www.ramapo.edu/publicsafety/how-to-apply-for-a-parking-permit/) [4](https://www.ramapo.edu/publicsafety/parking-regulations/) [6](https://www.ramapo.edu/publicsafety/parking-permits/) [9](https://www.ramapo.edu/student-accounts/parking/) [16](https://www.ramapo.edu/student-accounts/costinfo/) [21](https://www.ramapo.edu/campus-directory/)

question: is it too late to withdraw from a class this semester and what happens to my transcript if i do

body.answer:
That's a big decision, and it's worth talking it through with someone before you decide.

The Fall 2026 academic calendar lists [21]:
- Friday, October 2, 2026: Session I Courses - Last Day to Withdraw ("W" Grade) (already passed)
- Friday, November 6, 2026: Full Semester Courses – Last Day to Withdraw from Courses (“W” Grade) (already passed)
- Tuesday, November 24, 2026: Session II Courses - Last Day to Withdraw from Courses ("W" Grade)

It depends on the course session: the full-semester and Session I withdrawal deadlines listed above have passed; the Session II deadline is still ahead [21]. A student may not withdraw after the published deadline [6].

For a withdrawal within the deadline, use the online withdrawal form, complete a course withdrawal form at the Office of the Registrar, or withdraw online through Web Self Service. Once processed, a W appears for the course on your transcript [1].

If extraordinary circumstances prevented you from meeting the deadline, you may pursue a late administrative withdrawal. The Office of the Provost ordinarily expects an application before the semester ends; explain why you could not follow standard withdrawal procedures. The Provost or designee reviews the appeal and documentation; the burden of proof is yours. A granted appeal typically results in W grades for all courses in the term [2].

- **Registrar**: Phone: (201) 684-7695. Email: reg@ramapo.edu. Office: D-224. [22]
- **Office of the Provost**: Phone: (201) 684-7330. Email: provost@ramapo.edu. Location: first floor of the Birch Mansion. [22]

These offices can help:
- **Center for Student Success (Academic Advising)**: Phone: (201) 684-7441. Email: success@ramapo.edu. Office: D-207. [23]
- **Counseling Center**: Phone: (201) 684-7522. Office: D-216. [23]
- **Financial Aid**: Phone: (201) 684-7549. Email: finaid@ramapo.edu. Office: E-210. [23]

Sources: [1](https://catalog.ramapo.edu/pages/R532kjMfIcfnIkM0srb3#dropping-or-withdrawing-from-a-course1) [2](https://catalog.ramapo.edu/pages/R532kjMfIcfnIkM0srb3#withdrawal-or-leave-of-absence-from-the-college) [6](https://www.ramapo.edu/registrar/withdrawing-leave-of-absence/) [21](https://www.ramapo.edu/academic-calendars/) [22](https://www.ramapo.edu/campus-directory/) [23](https://www.ramapo.edu/campus-directory/)

Use the TMA iService Desk and Online Service Request Portal. \(page: “Using the TMA iService Desk: Online Service Request Portal \(https://ramapocollege.webtma.com/app/request/cb3dd15e-4c5a-435c-8c85-5d39c47951c6\)”\) 2. There is a phone in each area of rescue assistance that automatically dials Public Safety. Disabled persons should stay in this area and await help. question: My RA wrote me up for a candle. what happens now? do i have to go to a hearing

body.answer:
Residence Life lists candles as prohibited. Residence Life staff may confiscate prohibited items. [14] If the candle use activated a fire alarm due to disregard of a published policy, the listed 1st-offense outcome is a $150 fine and completion of a fire safety reflection assignment; the 2nd-offense outcome is a $300 fine, disciplinary probation, and possible suspension or loss of housing privileges. [2] Those outcomes are conditional on the fire-alarm activation described, not simply possession of a candle. [2]

If a disciplinary hearing is scheduled, you may submit signed, dated statements or documents to the Office of Student Conduct before the hearing, and you may request an appointment to review the statements and incident reports the complainant will use. You may have an advisor of your choosing, including an attorney, but the advisor cannot speak during the hearing. [1] The available pages don't say whether an RA write-up automatically leads to a hearing or whether you must attend one; contact the Office of Student Conduct to confirm what applies to your case. [1]

- **Housing & Residence Life**: Phone: (201) 684-7461. Email: reslife@ramapo.edu. [21]
- **Office of Student Conduct**: Phone: (201) 684-7869. Email: studentconduct@ramapo.edu. Office: C-212. [21]

Sources: [1](https://www.ramapo.edu/student-conduct/hearing/) [2](https://www.ramapo.edu/student-conduct/fire-safety/) [14](https://www.ramapo.edu/reslife/gtcl/) [21](https://www.ramapo.edu/campus-directory/)

question: I got a credit balance on my student account after my aid posted, how do I get that money sent to me? Do I need to sign up for direct deposit or does it just get mailed?

body.answer:
Student Accounts: Unless you specify otherwise, the College issues a paper check mailed to your billing/permanent address; checks are not mailed to campus mailboxes and cannot be picked up at the office. Direct deposit is free and is the fastest way to receive a refund. [1][10]

A refund is issued for a Title IV aid credit balance of $1.00 or greater; non-Title IV aid credit balances have a $5.00 threshold. [1]

To sign up: Log into RCNJ Experience; locate the Student Account Info card; click Bill & Payment Suite; click Electronic Refunds under My Profile Setup. Enroll in Two-Step Verification (skip if already completed): in My Profile, click Security Settings, select a passcode method (text message, email or Google Authentication), click Send Code, enter the passcode and click Verify. Click Payment Profile; edit or create a payment method, then check the Refund Option box to designate it for direct deposit. [4]

Once you sign up, an eligible refund is expected within one to two weeks of submitting the application. [3]

**Student Accounts**: Phone: (201) 684-7495. Email: studentaccts@ramapo.edu. Location: D-Wing, First Floor. [21]

Sources: [1](https://www.ramapo.edu/student-accounts/deposits/) [3](https://www.ramapo.edu/student-accounts/direct-deposit-questions-answers/) [4](https://www.ramapo.edu/student-accounts/direct-deposit/) [10](https://www.ramapo.edu/scholarships/faqs/) [21](https://www.ramapo.edu/campus-directory/)

question: how do i add my parent as an authorized user so they can pay my bill

body.answer:
Student Accounts says an Authorized User can make payments on your behalf. To add your parent: [4]
1. Log into [RCNJ Experience](https://experience.elluciancloud.com/rconj/).
2. Locate the Student Account Info card.
3. Click on Bill & Payment Suite link.
4. Click on Authorized Users located on the right side of the page in the My Profile Setup section.
5. Click on the Add Authorized User tab.
6. Enter the email address of the desired authorized user, answer questions, and click the Continue button.
7. Click I Agree box then the Continue button. [4]
If you want them only to make payments, select ‘No’ for both “View billing statement” and “View payment history.” [3] They will receive an email link to the Bill and Payment Suite with a user name and password. [3] An Authorized User does not have access to your stored payment methods or personal information, and adding one does not permit Student Accounts to discuss your financial records with them. To permit that discussion, submit an Office of Student Accounts FERPA Waiver Form. [1]

**Student Accounts**: Phone: (201) 684-7495. Email: studentaccts@ramapo.edu. Location: D-Wing, First Floor. [21]

question: how do i switch roommates? we're not getting along at all

body.answer:
Roommate problems are really common, and they can be worked out. Your RA is a good first step.

Housing & Residence Life says to visit the [Room Change Process](https://www.ramapo.edu/reslife/rcp/) page for step-by-step details. Submit a Room Change Request Form during an open room change period; the online form is linked on that page and is available during active room change periods. Review the full process and the Residence Life Events & Important Dates calendar to understand how a room change might affect you. Requests aren’t guaranteed; approval depends on available space and other factors, and professional Residence Life staff make the final decisions. If approved, prorated housing charges and any applicable meal-plan changes will be assessed and adjusted on your student account. [1][2][5]

**Housing & Residence Life**: Phone: (201) 684-7461. Email: reslife@ramapo.edu. [21]

This office can help:
**Ombuds Office**: Phone: (201) 684-7804. Email: jwoods1@ramapo.edu. [22]

question: can alumni still use career services and the library after graduating

body.answer:

question: how do i get a work study job on campus? i have it in my aid package but idk where to apply

body.answer:
The On-Campus Employment for Students office says to register on Handshake, search open positions using the keyword “RCNJ,” and apply to the hiring unit following that posting’s instructions. Contact the listed supervisor. Students awarded Federal Work-Study are given priority for Student Assistant positions. [5] Since you already have Work-Study in your aid package, look for positions on Handshake: [https://ramapo.joinhandshake.com/](https://ramapo.joinhandshake.com/). [5]

The office says FWS students may earn up to the award specified by the Financial Aid Office for the academic year. [3] For questions about your award, contact Financial Aid at finaid@ramapo.edu. [5]

After accepting an offered position, you and your supervisor sign an employment form with your beginning work date, salary, etc. Return all copies of the required paperwork—the New hire packet, W-4 Form and I-9 Form—to the Student Assistant Program Office in Room D-119. [1] For onboarding questions, email SAP@ramapo.edu. [14]

**On-Campus Employment for Students**: Phone: (201) 684-7654. Email: sap@ramapo.edu. Office: D-119. [21]

Sources: [1](https://www.ramapo.edu/on-campus-employment/policies-and-procedures/) [3](https://www.ramapo.edu/on-campus-employment/) [5](https://www.ramapo.edu/on-campus-employment/) [14](https://www.ramapo.edu/budget/student-aid-budget-management/) [21](https://www.ramapo.edu/campus-directory/)

question: how do i find out why my financial aid hasnt shown up yet and who do i talk to

body.answer:
I can't see your personal records, like your grades, balance, schedule or financial aid status.

If your aid appears as a Memo, it has not met all requirements for payment; Student Accounts strongly recommends contacting the Office of Financial Aid to resolve outstanding issues [2]. Check your Ramapo College email regularly for financial aid correspondence [10].

The Office of Financial Aid can be contacted by email or through the chat on its website to make an in-person appointment. The office says most questions can also be handled by phone, Webex, or email; its page lists appointment hours [11].
