question: How do I set up a payment plan for spring semester tuition? and is there a fee to enroll in it

body.answer:
Student Accounts offers four- and five-month plans for Spring 2027. To enroll, “Log into RCNJ Experience (Web Self-Service)” ([https://experience.elluciancloud.com/rconj/](https://experience.elluciancloud.com/rconj/)), “Locate the Student Account Info card,” “Click on Bill & Payment Suite,” then “Click on the Payment Plans tab at the top of the screen or the ‘Enroll in’” [1]. The page’s instruction ends there.

The five-month plan’s down payment is available November 16–December 4, 2026; installments are due January 15, February 15, March 15 and April 15, 2027. The four-month plan’s down payment is available November 16, 2026–February 14, 2027; installments are due February 15, March 15 and April 15, 2027 [1]. You must pay the down payment and fee when enrolling. If enrolling after the down-payment due date, missed installments are also due then. Past-due balances from previous semesters of $500 or more must be paid before you’re eligible; enrollment may be denied based on past payment history. Missing the payment deadline may result in a $200 late fee and/or deregistration [1].

The enrollment fee is non-refundable and $60; the plans do not charge interest [1][2].

**Student Accounts**: Phone: (201) 684-7495. Email: studentaccts@ramapo.edu. Location: D-Wing, First Floor. [21]

Sources: [1](https://www.ramapo.edu/student-accounts/options-policies/) [2](https://www.ramapo.edu/student-accounts/faq/) [21](https://www.ramapo.edu/campus-directory/)

question: whats the deadline to file the FAFSA for next year and what does ramapo need from me besides that

body.answer:
For the 2027–2028 FAFSA, the deadline is April 1 for returning students and May 1 for new students. The FAFSA is open, and new students should submit by May 1 so Ramapo can send an award letter around June 1. [14] Ramapo’s FAFSA school code is 009344; apply at [https://studentaid.gov/h/apply-for-aid/fafsa](https://studentaid.gov/h/apply-for-aid/fafsa). [1] Ramapo also says students must complete all forms in a timely manner, but the pages here don’t identify any additional forms for everyone. [3] An older FAFSA page, updated July 2025, gives March 15 as the new-student deadline. [12]

**Financial Aid**: Phone: (201) 684-7549. Email: finaid@ramapo.edu. Office: E-210. [21]

The Registrar page says a student may NOT withdraw after the published deadline [12]. If you are asking about an exception, the Office of the Provost describes a late administrative withdrawal under extraordinary circumstances: explain why you could not follow standard withdrawal procedures or request incompletes, identify the term, and ordinarily apply before semester end (or explain why you could not). The Provost or designee reviews your appeal letter and documentation and decides whether to accept it; the burden of proof is yours. A granted request typically results in W grades for all courses in the term. [9] The catalog’s course-withdrawal policy says withdrawing after the 50% refund period is possible only through the last day to withdraw shown on the academic calendar, using an online withdrawal form, a course withdrawal form completed at the Registrar, or Web Self Service; after the form is processed, you receive a W. [8]

The catalog says withdrawal may affect financial aid eligibility and satisfactory progress toward graduation. [8] The Office of Financial Aid recommends discussing any class withdrawal with it to determine the impact on your current aid package. [1][23] Federal aid should not be affected if you remain enrolled in 6 or more credits; NJ State aid requires full-time enrollment when aid is fully disbursed. [23] Aid may be adjusted if you fall below full-time: Pell may be reduced, loans can be kept at 6 credits, and state aid, institutional grants or scholarships may be reduced or canceled. [3] For SAP, financial-aid eligibility requires completing at least 67% of attempted credits; undergraduate GPA must be at least 2.0 and graduate GPA 3.0 at the annual review after spring. [2]

The Office of the Registrar’s page says no withdrawal after the published deadline; the catalog describes late administrative withdrawal only for extraordinary circumstances. [12][9]

question: my roommate keeps having his girlfriend sleep over like 5 nights a week. is there a guest policy and who do i talk to about it

body.answer:
Roommate problems are really common, and they can be worked out. Your RA is a good first step.

Yes. The current Guest Procedures say roommates should discuss guest expectations; you can contact your Resident Assistant to opt out of automatic guest registration and arrange a roommate contract. If the contract is violated, staff in your hall/area office need a formal complaint before they can act. The policy does not state a general five-nights-per-week limit; it says guests may not move from host to host to stay on campus more than three nights. [3]
If she is 18 or older and not assigned to on-campus housing, she must complete Guest Registration if visiting after 10 PM; guests must stay with their hosts and have the approved registration email and valid ID. [24]
Talk to your RA first, or the staff in your hall/area office. Overnight guests are not permitted on campus after Monday, December 14, 2026. [6]

**Housing & Residence Life**: Phone: (201) 684-7461. Email: reslife@ramapo.edu. [33]

This office can help:
**Ombuds Office**: Phone: (201) 684-7804. Email: jwoods1@ramapo.edu. [34]

Sources: [3](https://www.ramapo.edu/reslife/gtcl/) [6](https://www.ramapo.edu/reslife/fallcheckoutandwinter/) [24](https://www.ramapo.edu/reslife/gtcl/) [33](https://www.ramapo.edu/campus-directory/) [34](https://www.ramapo.edu/campus-directory/)

question: how do i get a parking permit and how much does it cost

body.answer:
Public Safety says to ensure the parking fee has been applied to your RCNJ student account, then visit [Parking Permits](https://www.ramapo.edu/publicsafety/parking-permits/) [4]. The permit application is online only [9].

Orientation Programs’ instructions: Log on to the RCNJ Parking Permits website; “Enter Permit Type and click Continue.” Complete the Contact Information page, click “Save/Update Person” and then “Continue.” Enter Vehicle Information and click “Continue.” Review your request and click “Continue.” Print or save the Registration Filed page with your registration request number as verification; it is not your permit. Select the correct housing assignment or commuter status, and select “student,” not “faculty/staff” [1].

New students pick up permits during New Student Check-In; returning residents get them from their on-campus mailbox; returning commuters pick them up at the Public Safety ID Office Monday through Friday during normal operating hours, or at the Public Safety Office Main Desk after 3 pm if they email parkingpermits@ramapo.edu to request another pick-up time [1,4].

For 2026–2027, the Fall/Spring permit (valid through Spring 2027) is $250.00. Off-campus students are charged a $16.58 commuter parking tax; resident students have a $50.00 resident parking supplement. Spring-only (new student): $125.00, plus $8.29 commuter tax or $25.00 resident supplement. Summer-only: $100.00, plus $6.63 commuter tax [16].

The older Orientation FAQ (updated July 2022) gives different application instructions [2].

- **Public Safety (Non-Emergency)**: Phone: (201) 684-7432. Email: publicsafety@ramapo.edu. Office: C-102. [21]
- **Public Safety (Emergency)**: Phone: (201) 684-6666. Email: publicsafety@ramapo.edu. Office: C-102. [21]
- **Orientation Programs**: Phone: (201) 684-7441. Email: orient@ramapo.edu. Office: D-207. [21]

question: is it too late to withdraw from a class this semester and what happens to my transcript if i do

body.answer:
That's a big decision, and it's worth talking it through with someone before you decide.

The Fall 2026 academic calendar lists [21]:
- Friday, October 2, 2026: Session I Courses - Last Day to Withdraw ("W" Grade) (already passed)
- Friday, November 6, 2026: Full Semester Courses – Last Day to Withdraw from Courses (“W” Grade) (already passed)
- Tuesday, November 24, 2026: Session II Courses - Last Day to Withdraw from Courses ("W" Grade)

It depends on the course session: the full-semester withdrawal deadline has passed, but the Session II deadline is still upcoming [21]. A student may not withdraw after the published deadline [6].

Before your course’s deadline, you can use the online withdrawal form, complete a course withdrawal form in the Office of the Registrar, or withdraw online through Web Self Service [1]. Once the Registrar processes it, you receive a W for the course, and you and your instructor of record are notified [1]. If you have a registration hold, you can use the Withdrawal Form or email reg@ramapo.edu from your Ramapo email, stating your first and last name, Ramapo ID (R#), CRN, subject, course number, section number, and course title [6].

If extraordinary circumstances prevented you from meeting the deadline, you may apply for a late administrative withdrawal. Ordinarily, apply before the semester ends; explain why you could not follow standard withdrawal procedures or request an incomplete, and identify the term. Supporting documentation may include medical-provider documentation, a death certificate, relevant medical documentation and proof of caregiving, documentation of relocation due to a natural disaster, or an employer’s dated letter requiring immediate relocation. The Provost or designee reviews the appeal and documentation and decides whether to accept it; they may request a meeting or more information. If granted, typically you receive W grades in all courses for the term [2][7].

**Registrar**: Phone: (201) 684-7695. Email: reg@ramapo.edu. Office: D-224. [22]

These offices can help:
- **Center for Student Success (Academic Advising)**: Phone: (201) 684-7441. Email: success@ramapo.edu. Office: D-207. [23]
- **Counseling Center**: Phone: (201) 684-7522. Office: D-216. [23]
- **Financial Aid**: Phone: (201) 684-7549. Email: finaid@ramapo.edu. Office: E-210. [23]

Sources: [1](https://catalog.ramapo.edu/pages/R532kjMfIcfnIkM0srb3#dropping-or-withdrawing-from-a-course1) [2](https://catalog.ramapo.edu/pages/R532kjMfIcfnIkM0srb3#withdrawal-or-leave-of-absence-from-the-college) [6](https://www.ramapo.edu/registrar/withdrawing-leave-of-absence/) [7](https://www.ramapo.edu/registrar/withdrawing-leave-of-absence/) [21](https://www.ramapo.edu/academic-calendars/) [22](https://www.ramapo.edu/campus-directory/) [23](https://www.ramapo.edu/campus-directory/)

value.heading: Get an immediate response to imminent danger
value.text: 1. If a student or the community is in imminent danger, contact Public Safety at (201) 684-6666. (page: “If there is an imminent danger to a student, or to the community, contact the Public Safety Department at (201) 684-6666.”)
value.section_words: An online Report Form for Sexual Misconduct (https://publicdocs.maxient.com/reportingform.php?RamapoCollege&layout_id=9) is also available. The form may be filled out anonymously, or the survivor may choose to include identifying information. Submissions are read and responded to during regular business hours. This form is not to be used for emergencies that require an immediate response. If there is an imminent danger to a student, or to the community, contact the Public Safety Department at (201) 684-6666.
value.page_words: REPORTING TO THE MAHWAH POLICE DEPARTMENT: The Mahwah Police Department (http://www.mahwahpd.org/)can be reached by calling (201) 529-1000 or by calling 911. If a sexual assault took place within the past 5 days the responding officer will activate the Bergen County Sexual Assault Response Team (SART). SART is a free, coordinated community response to assist a survivor in the aftermath of a recent sexual assault. It has been designed to offer a compassionate, victim-centered approach while collecting evidence that can be vital to the investigation and prosecution of the crime. SART is available 24 hours a day, 7 days a week There are three members of the SART team available to a survivor. A survivor has the option to speak with all three SART members, any combination of SART members, or speak with none of the SART members. SART members include: Forensic Nurse Examiner (FNE): A FNE is specially trained in forensic evidence collection. The FNE conducts a head to toe exam and collects evidence to assist in the prosecution of the crime. Medications to prevent Sexually Transmitted Infections and pregnancy resulting from the sexual assault are also offered to the survivor. The FNE does not treat injury; anyone needing medical attention will be seen by the attending physician in the local Emergency Department. Law Enforcement: A local police officer and/or detective from the Bergen

value.heading: Request a campus safety escort
value.text: 1. You can arrange an escort any time of day if you need to be accompanied from one campus location to another. (page: “If you need to be accompanied from one point to another, you can arrange for a personal safety escort any time of day.”) 2. Call Public Safety at 201- 684 -6666, or use a blue light telephone or other security phone box. (page: “Call the Public Safety Department at 201- 684 -6666 or from the blue light telephones or other security phone boxes.”) 3. Tell the operator your name, exact location, destination, and callback telephone number. (page: “Tell the operator your name and exact location, destination, and a call back telephone number.”) 4. Wait for an officer; an emergency situation may cause a longer wait. (page: “An officer will be dispatched and respond as soon as possible. In most instances the officer will respond in a timely manner, however an emergency situation may dictate a longer waiting period for the escort.”) 5. Walk in pairs or small groups, especially late at night. (page: “We strongly encourage you to walk in pairs or small groups especially late at night.”)
value.section_words: Call the Public Safety Department at 201- 684 -6666 or from the blue light telephones or other security phone boxes. Tell the operator your name and exact location, destination, and a call back telephone number. An officer will be dispatched and respond as soon as possible. In most instances the officer will respond in a timely manner, however an emergency situation may dictate a longer waiting period for the escort. Please be patient.
value.page_words: Campus Safety Escorts: We want you to feel safe anywhere you go on campus. A Safety Escort Service is available for individuals who not feel safe walking alone on campus. If you need to be accompanied from one point to another, you can arrange for a personal safety escort any time of day. We strongly encourage you to walk in pairs or small groups especially late at night. Inappropriate use of the service takes Public Safety away from regular patrol and campus safety issues. To schedule a safety escort pick-up:: Call the Public Safety Department at 201- 684 -6666 or from the blue light telephones or other security phone boxes. Tell the operator your name and exact location, destination, and a call back telephone number. An officer will be dispatched and respond as soon as possible. In most instances the officer will respond in a timely manner, however an emergency situation may dictate a longer waiting period for the escort. Please be patient. Restrictions:: The safety escort service is not intended to be a taxi service. Students who display disruptive behavior may not use this service. Public Safety reserves the right to refuse service to disruptive individuals. No pets or animals allowed except for service animals. The number of passengers allowed is determined by the vehicle capacity, but is generally limited to three (3) passengers
value.applies_to: Individuals who do not feel safe walking alone on campus

value.page_words: If you require immediate assistance, problems such as no power, elevator malfunctions, plumbing leaks/clogs, no heat/AC any lock related problem, or health safety concerns please call the Service Desk at extension 7660, Monday through Friday, 8:00 AM to 4:30 PM or Public Safety after these hours at extension 6666. If utilizing the online system on your own, please send only one request per issue. Our system will send automatic email notifications to the sender when the request is processed, when the status changes and when the work is complete. If you have any questions or concerns regarding your request, you may call our Service Desk at extension 7660; please reference the request number generated by the system when you call. return to top Asbestos: The College Park apartments were built before 1980, and some of their construction materials contain asbestos. Buckeye, Holly, International, Mimosa, Elm, Palm, Redwood, Hickory, Science, Mulberry, and Cypress have been renovated and are asbestos-free. Materials that contain asbestos include floor tiles/mastic and joint compound in walls and ceilings. These materials present no hazard unless they are impaired or disturbed. Puncturing these materials could cause a release of asbestos fibers. Please do not insert nails, tacks, hooks or otherwise impair or disturb the materials. If you notice any damage, please vacate the apartment

Hours: Monday to Friday: 7:30am-4:30pm; Saturday and Sunday: Not published. Start date: not published. End date: not published. Published note: Administrative Offices Monday - Friday, 7:30 a.m. to 4:30 p.m. [campus-hours](https://www.ramapo.edu/facilities/)

Contact note: You can submit a request using any of the following methods: Using the TMA iService Desk: Online Service Request Portal By Telephone: 201-684-7660 For Media, ITS and Telecomm requests please visit https://helpdesk.ramapo.edu/ If you require immediate assistance, problems such as no power, elevator malfunctions, plumbing leaks/clogs, no heat/AC any lock related problem, or health safety concerns please call the Service Desk at extension 7660. Any emergencies that occur between 4:30 p.m. and 7:30 a.m. OR on weekends should be reported to Public Safety at extension 6666. How-to and policies: Get immediate assistance for an urgent Facilities problem: 1. For no power, elevator malfunctions, plumbing leaks or clogs, no heat or AC, lock problems, or health and safety concerns, call the Service Desk at extension 7660. \(page: “If you require immediate assistance, problems such as no power, elevator malfunctions, plumbing leaks/clogs, no heat/AC any lock related problem, or health safety concerns please call the Service Desk at extension 7660.”\) (see https://www.ramapo.edu/facilities/service-guide/) [office-pages](https://www.ramapo.edu/facilities/service-guide/)

How-to and policies: Report an after-hours or weekend emergency: 1. Report emergencies occurring between 4:30 p.m. and 7:30 a.m., or on weekends, to Public Safety at extension 6666. \(page: “Any emergencies that occur between 4:30 p.m. and 7:30 a.m. OR on weekends should be reported to Public Safety at extension 6666.”\) (see https://www.ramapo.edu/facilities/service-guide/) [office-pages](https://www.ramapo.edu/facilities/service-guide/)

How-to and policies: Submit a Facilities work request: 1. Use the TMA iService Desk and Online Service Request Portal. \(page: “Using the TMA iService Desk: Online Service Request Portal \(https://ramapocollege.webtma.com/app/request/cb3dd15e-4c5a-435c-8c85-5d39c47951c6\)”\) 2. Call 201-684-7660. \(page: “By Telephone: 201-684-7660”\) (see https://www.ramapo.edu/facilities/service-request-portal/) [office-pages](https://www.ramapo.edu/facilities/service-request-portal/)

How-to and policies: Request routine Facilities service: 1. Submit a service request using the Service Request Form. \(page: “To request services click on the button below. Service Request Form \(https://ramapocollege.webtma.com/app/request/d4d71f56-79f4-47b2-98d6-5a7b536b4f2a\)”\) 2. Routine work requests are scheduled by the Supervisors. \(page: “Routine work requests are scheduled by the Supervisors.”\) (see https://www.ramapo.edu/facilities/service-guide/) [office-pages](https://www.ramapo.edu/facilities/service-guide/)

question: whats my current balance and do i have any holds on my account

body.answer:
I can't see your personal records, like your grades, balance, schedule or financial aid status.

I don’t have verified information about your individual balance or holds. The Office of Student Accounts says the Bill & Payment Suite in RCNJ Experience (Web Self-Service) shows current, real-time account activity and balances. Log in at [https://experience.elluciancloud.com/rconj/](https://experience.elluciancloud.com/rconj/) and open the Bill & Payment Suite to view your account. [24]

Student Accounts says students with an unpaid outstanding balance will have a Hold Flag, which is removed once the account is paid in full. A hold from another office or department may still prevent registration. The pages don’t explain how to check all holds in the account, so contact Student Accounts for help verifying yours. [3]

**Student Accounts**: Phone: (201) 684-7495. Email: studentaccts@ramapo.edu. Location: D-Wing, First Floor. [33]

Sources: [3](https://www.ramapo.edu/student-accounts/payment-policies/) [24](https://www.ramapo.edu/student-accounts/billpolicies/) [33](https://www.ramapo.edu/campus-directory/)

question: My RA wrote me up for a candle. what happens now? do i have to go to a hearing

body.answer:
Candles are prohibited in residences. Residence Life staff address prohibited-item violations, and Residence Life staff, Public Safety, or the College Fire Marshal may confiscate prohibited items they find. [14]

The listed sanctions apply if the candle resulted in a fire-alarm activation due to disregard of policy: a first offense is a $150 fine and Fire Safety Reflection assignment; a second is a $300 fine, disciplinary probation, and possible suspension or loss of housing privileges. [2] This page does not say that merely possessing a candle carries those sanctions. [2]

The pages don’t say what happens after an RA write-up or whether your case requires a hearing, so I can’t verify if you must attend one. The Office of Student Conduct is the right office to ask about your case. If you are preparing for a hearing, you may review the written statements and incident reports to be used; contact the office to arrange an appointment or request the file. You may have an advisor of your choice at a hearing, but they cannot speak during it. [1]

- **Housing & Residence Life**: Phone: (201) 684-7461. Email: reslife@ramapo.edu. [21]
- **Office of Student Conduct**: Phone: (201) 684-7869. Email: studentconduct@ramapo.edu. Office: C-212. [21]

Sources: [1](https://www.ramapo.edu/student-conduct/hearing/) [2](https://www.ramapo.edu/student-conduct/fire-safety/) [14](https://www.ramapo.edu/reslife/gtcl/) [21](https://www.ramapo.edu/campus-directory/)

question: I got a credit balance on my student account after my aid posted, how do I get that money sent to me? Do I need to sign up for direct deposit or does it just get mailed?

body.answer:
Student Accounts: Unless you specify otherwise, the College issues a paper check mailed to your billing/permanent address; checks are not sent to campus mailboxes and cannot be picked up at the office. A Title IV financial aid overpayment credit balance of $1.00 or greater is refunded; non-Title IV financial aid credit balances have a $5.00 threshold. [1]

Direct deposit is optional, free, and deposits a refund into your checking or savings account. To enroll, follow “Log into RCNJ Experience,” locate the Student Account Info card, click Bill & Payment Suite, then Electronic Refunds under My Profile Setup. Enroll in Two-Step Verification if needed; under Security Settings select a passcode method, send and verify the code. In Payment Profile, edit or create a payment method and check the box in Refund Option. [1][3] The page says an eligible refund can be deposited within one to two weeks after submitting the application. [2]

For help finding your checking/savings account and routing numbers, visit Student Accounts, first floor, D-Wing. [2]

**Student Accounts**: Phone: (201) 684-7495. Email: studentaccts@ramapo.edu. Location: D-Wing, First Floor. [21]

Sources: [1](https://www.ramapo.edu/student-accounts/deposits/) [2](https://www.ramapo.edu/student-accounts/direct-deposit-questions-answers/) [3](https://www.ramapo.edu/student-accounts/direct-deposit/) [21](https://www.ramapo.edu/campus-directory/)

question: how do i add my parent as an authorized user so they can pay my bill

body.answer:
Student Accounts: Log into [RCNJ Experience](https://experience.elluciancloud.com/rconj/), locate the Student Account Info card, click “Bill & Payment Suite,” then “Authorized Users” on the right side of the page in the My Profile Setup section. Click “Add Authorized User,” enter your parent’s email address, answer the questions, and click “Continue.” Click the “I Agree” box, then “Continue.” [4]

If you want them to make payments only, select “No” for both “View billing statement” and “View payment history.” [3] Authorized Users can make payments on your behalf, but they do not have access to your stored payment methods or other personal information. [1] [5]

If you also want Student Accounts to discuss your financial records with your parent, submit the [Registrar’s Office FERPA Waiver form](https://www.ramapo.edu/catalog/registration-policies/?ferpa=open). [6] An older Authorized Users page, updated March 2026, instead names an Office of Student Accounts FERPA Waiver Form. [1]

question: how do i set up my campus email and wifi login

body.answer:
The Registrar says new students should visit [https://password.ramapo.edu/](https://password.ramapo.edu/) and click “Activate E-mail Account.” You can set up the account within 24 hours of receiving your Ramapo ID number. [8]

The IT Help Desk says MFA is required for Ramapo Gmail. On a new device, verify your identity using the Gmail app on your phone; tap to approve the login. Trust only devices you own, never public or shared computers. [4][2]

ResNET says you need a valid Ramapo email account and a device with wireless or wired connectivity. Register the device you plan to use before it can access the college network; a registered device can be used campus-wide. [6][3] First determine whether you will use wired or wireless, then retrieve the MAC address for that connection using [https://www.ramapo.edu/resnet/getmac/](https://www.ramapo.edu/resnet/getmac/). [15] Register at [https://resnet.ramapo.edu/register/login.php](https://resnet.ramapo.edu/register/login.php) for wired or [http://mydevices.ramapo.edu/](http://mydevices.ramapo.edu/) for wireless. [14] To connect wirelessly, scan for wireless networks on your device and connect. [17]

- **Registrar**: Phone: (201) 684-7695. Email: reg@ramapo.edu. Office: D-224. [21]

question: how do i switch roommates? we're not getting along at all

body.answer:
Roommate problems are really common, and they can be worked out. Your RA is a good first step.

Housing & Residence Life handles room changes. Submit a Room Change Request Form during an open room change period. Review the full process and instructions at [https://www.ramapo.edu/reslife/rcp/](https://www.ramapo.edu/reslife/rcp/) and check the Residence Life Events & Important Dates calendar to understand how a room change might affect you. The online form is at [https://docs.google.com/forms/d/e/1FAIpQLSflQtcwyqtigPCfHGI4IOscg7Zfp10vRzMMR34xv7_MDjyb6A/viewform?usp=dialog](https://docs.google.com/forms/d/e/1FAIpQLSflQtcwyqtigPCfHGI4IOscg7Zfp10vRzMMR34xv7_MDjyb6A/viewform?usp=dialog). Room changes are not guaranteed; they depend on available space and other factors, and professional Residence Life staff make the final decision. [1][2][5]
If approved, housing charges are prorated and adjusted, and any applicable meal-plan changes are assessed and adjusted on your student account. Review housing and meal-plan costs through the Office of Student Accounts: [https://www.ramapo.edu/student-accounts](https://www.ramapo.edu/student-accounts). [2] Approved residents with current parking permits must return the old permit at the Office of Public Safety (ID room) to receive a new one and update parking information, if applicable. [3]
For unresolved conflict, Residence Life reserves the right to reassign students to another space. [4]

**Housing & Residence Life**: Phone: (201) 684-7461. Email: reslife@ramapo.edu. [21]

This office can help:
**Ombuds Office**: Phone: (201) 684-7804. Email: jwoods1@ramapo.edu. [22]

Sources: [1](https://www.ramapo.edu/reslife/gtcl/) [2](https://www.ramapo.edu/reslife/new-student-guide/) [3](https://www.ramapo.edu/reslife/rcp/) [4](https://www.ramapo.edu/reslife/gtcl/) [5](https://www.ramapo.edu/reslife/rcp/) [21](https://www.ramapo.edu/campus-directory/) [22](https://www.ramapo.edu/campus-directory/)

question: can alumni still use career services and the library after graduating

body.answer:
Yes. The Office of Alumni Relations says alumni can access the Cahill Career Center’s services on the Ramapo campus, including help with job searches, resume updates and interviewing skills. For more information, contact the Cahill Career Center at (201) 684-7444 or careercenter@ramapo.edu. [2]

question: How do I set up a payment plan for spring semester tuition? and is there a fee to enroll in it

body.answer:
Student Accounts offers four- and five-month plans for Spring 2027. To enroll: “Log into RCNJ Experience (Web Self-Service)” ([https://experience.elluciancloud.com/rconj/](https://experience.elluciancloud.com/rconj/)), “Locate the Student Account Info card,” “Click on Bill & Payment Suite,” then “Click on the Payment Plans tab at the top of the screen.” [1] The page’s enrollment instructions continue at [https://www.ramapo.edu/student-accounts/options-policies/](https://www.ramapo.edu/student-accounts/options-policies/). [1]

The five-month plan’s down payment is available November 16–December 4, 2026; installments are due January 15, February 15, March 15 and April 15, 2027. The four-month plan’s down payment is available November 16, 2026–February 14, 2027; installments are due February 15, March 15 and April 15, 2027. [1]

Pay the down payment and a non-refundable $60 set-up fee when you enroll. [1] You must enroll and make your first installment before the semester’s payment deadline. Late enrollment requires payment of missed installments; past-due balances from previous semesters of $500 or more must be paid before you’re eligible. The College may deny enrollment based on past payment history. [1, 2] Installments are due by the 15th of each month; late payments incur a $35 fee. [1] For questions, contact Student Accounts.

**Student Accounts**: Phone: (201) 684-7495. Email: studentaccts@ramapo.edu. Location: D-Wing, First Floor. [21]

Sources: [1](https://www.ramapo.edu/student-accounts/options-policies/) [2](https://www.ramapo.edu/student-accounts/faq/) [21](https://www.ramapo.edu/campus-directory/)

question: refund

body.answer:
Student Accounts: A Title IV financial aid overpayment that leaves a credit balance of $1.00 or greater will be refunded. Credit balances from non-Title IV financial aid have a $5.00 threshold. Unless you specify otherwise, the College issues a paper check, mailed to your billing/permanent address; checks are not mailed to campus mailboxes or available for pickup at Student Accounts. [1]

If entitled to a fall-term refund, you may ask to have it applied to spring by emailing studentaccts@ramapo.edu. Spring refunds cannot be applied to the following fall term. [1]

Electronic/direct deposit is free. Sign up at [https://www.ramapo.edu/student-accounts/direct-deposit/](https://www.ramapo.edu/student-accounts/direct-deposit/); details are at [https://www.ramapo.edu/student-accounts/direct-deposit-questions-answers/](https://www.ramapo.edu/student-accounts/direct-deposit-questions-answers/). [1] To set it up: log into RCNJ Experience; open the Student Account Info card, then Bill & Payment Suite, then Electronic Refunds under My Profile Setup. Enroll in Two-Step Verification if needed: in My Profile, open Security Settings, choose a passcode method, send and verify the code. Open Payment Profile, edit or create a payment method, and check the box in Refund Option to designate it for direct deposit. [6]

**Student Accounts**: Phone: (201) 684-7495. Email: studentaccts@ramapo.edu. Location: D-Wing, First Floor. [21]

question: what is the policy on withdrawing from a class after the deadline and does it affect my aid/satisfactory academic progress

body.answer:
The Fall 2026 academic calendar lists [21]:
- Friday, October 2, 2026: Session I Courses - Last Day to Withdraw ("W" Grade) (already passed)
- Friday, November 6, 2026: Full Semester Courses – Last Day to Withdraw from Courses (“W” Grade) (already passed)
- Tuesday, November 24, 2026: Session II Courses - Last Day to Withdraw from Courses ("W" Grade)

The Registrar says a student may NOT withdraw after the published deadline; see the Academic Calendar [12]. For an individual course, the catalog says withdrawal is allowed after the 50% refund period only through the last day to withdraw [8].

A possible exception is a late administrative withdrawal under extraordinary circumstances. The student should explain why standard procedures could not be followed (or why incompletes were not requested or granted), identify the term, and ordinarily apply before semester’s end. The Provost or designee reviews the appeal letter and supporting documentation; the burden of proof is on the student. They may request a meeting or more information. Examples of documentation include specified medical-provider records, a family member’s death certificate, medical-care documentation, natural-disaster relocation documentation, or an employer’s dated relocation letter [13].

Withdrawing can affect financial-aid eligibility and progress toward graduation [8]. Financial Aid says official withdrawal or leaving school before 60% of a semester concludes is subject to federal rules on retaining or returning Title IV aid; that page specifically discusses withdrawing from all classes. It recommends meeting with Financial Aid about the effect on your current aid package [1]. Dropping below full-time may adjust aid; federal aid requires 6 credits, and state aid, institutional grants or scholarships could be reduced or canceled [3]. Academic scholarships or Ramapo grants may also be reduced or taken away below 12 credits [5].

SAP is reviewed annually after spring. Students must complete at least 67% of credits attempted; the policy also sets a 2.0 undergraduate or 3.0 graduate cumulative GPA standard [2]. Graduate students receiving federal aid should consult Financial Aid because federal SAP may differ from the College’s academic-progress rules [11]. Your individual aid/SAP impact depends on your circumstances; consult Financial Aid. For the withdrawal process and extraordinary-circumstances exception, contact the Registrar [12][13].

- **Registrar**: Phone: (201) 684-7695. Email: reg@ramapo.edu. Office: D-224. [22]
- **Financial Aid**: Phone: (201) 684-7549. Email: finaid@ramapo.edu. Office: E-210. [22]

Sources: [1](https://www.ramapo.edu/finaid/faqs/) [2](https://www.ramapo.edu/finaid/policies/) [3](https://www.ramapo.edu/finaid/faqs/) [5](https://www.ramapo.edu/finaid/academic-merit-scholarships-terms-conditions/) [8](https://catalog.ramapo.edu/pages/R532kjMfIcfnIkM0srb3#dropping-or-withdrawing-from-a-course1) [11](https://catalog.ramapo.edu/pages/R532kjMfIcfnIkM0srb3#graduate-student-academic-progress) [12](https://www.ramapo.edu/registrar/withdrawing-leave-of-absence/) [13](https://www.ramapo.edu/registrar/withdrawing-leave-of-absence/) [21](https://www.ramapo.edu/academic-calendars/) [22](https://www.ramapo.edu/campus-directory/)

Ramapo says it provides a 1098-T to students who incurred qualified tuition and related expenses and paid corresponding payments during the tax year; the form is provided each year on or before January 31 and reports the prior tax year. The form will be printed within 5–7 business days and mailed to the home address on file with the Registrar’s Office. question: im a transfer student and i commute, how do i get a parking permit and where do i park

body.answer:
To apply, go to [RCNJ Parking Permits](https://www.ramapo.edu/publicsafety/parking-permits/) and follow the Parking Permit Application Instructions. Log on to the site; enter Permit Type and click Continue; complete Contact Information and click Save/Update Person, then Continue; enter Vehicle Information and Continue; review your request and Continue; then print or save the Registration Filed page with your request number as application verification. That page is not your permit. Select the correct commuter status. New students pick up permits at New Student Check-In; returning commuter students pick them up at the Public Safety ID Office during weekday operating hours. [1] Commuters may register two vehicles on one permit, but only one registered vehicle may be on campus at a time. [12]

Commuters receive a rearview-mirror hangtag and should “Park in the appropriate lot.” See [parking regulations](https://www.ramapo.edu/publicsafety/parking-regulations/). Commuters may not park overnight (2am–6am) without prior Public Safety authorization. [14][15] The information provided does not identify which specific lot is appropriate for commuters; contact Public Safety to confirm.

- **Orientation Programs**: Phone: (201) 684-7441. Email: orient@ramapo.edu. Office: D-207. [21]
- **Public Safety (Non-Emergency)**: Phone: (201) 684-7432. Email: publicsafety@ramapo.edu. Office: C-102. [21]
- **Public Safety (Emergency)**: Phone: (201) 684-6666. Email: publicsafety@ramapo.edu. Office: C-102. [21]

Sources: [1](https://www.ramapo.edu/orientation/faq-2/) [12](https://www.ramapo.edu/publicsafety/parking-regulations/) [14](https://www.ramapo.edu/publicsafety/how-to-apply-for-a-parking-permit/) [15](https://www.ramapo.edu/publicsafety/parking-regulations/) [21](https://www.ramapo.edu/campus-directory/)

question: I'm a commuter student and I have a 3 hour gap between classes. Is there somewhere on campus I can study or hang out, like a commuter lounge, and is there a way to store my stuff?

The Center for Student Involvement says J. Lee’s is the unofficial Commuter Lounge, on the second floor of the Student Center between the Student Government and Black Student Union offices. question: what is the deadline to drop a class without a W and how do i do it

body.answer:
I can't send messages or make changes for you, like registering, dropping a class or making a payment.

The Fall 2026 academic calendar lists [21]:
- Friday, August 28, 2026: Session I Courses - Last Day of Add/Drop for 100% Tuition Refund (already passed)
- Tuesday, September 1, 2026: Full Semester Courses - Last Day of Add/Drop for 100% Tuition Refund (already passed)
- Wednesday, October 21, 2026: Session II Courses - Last Day to Add/Drop for 100% Tuition Refund (already passed)

The no-W deadline is the last day of the Add/Drop period for your course/session; check the academic calendar for the applicable term. The Fall 2026 dates are already listed above. [3] [2]

The Registrar says to drop the course in Web Self Service by that deadline; courses dropped there through and including the last Add/Drop day will not appear on your transcript. question: my roommate keeps having his girlfriend sleep over like 5 nights a week. is there a guest policy and who do i talk to about it

body.answer:
Roommate problems are really common, and they can be worked out. Your RA is a good first step.

Yes. Guests may not move from host to host to stay on campus more than three (3) nights. Residents are responsible for their guests, and roommates should discuss guest expectations and alert the host to concerns. To set expectations, contact your Resident Assistant to facilitate a roommate/suitemate/apartment contract. If someone violates that contract, hall/area office staff need a formal complaint before they can act; all residents of the space may lose guest privileges while a contract is developed. [3]
The latest overnight-guest notice says the last night residents may host overnight guests is Monday, December 14, 2026; none are permitted after that date, and residents with an approved check-out extension may not have guests. [6] For a violation of the Guide to Community Living, the responsible office is the Office of Residence Life. [16]

question: is it too late to withdraw from a class this semester and what happens to my transcript if i do

body.answer:
That's a big decision, and it's worth talking it through with someone before you decide.

The Fall 2026 academic calendar lists [21]:
- Friday, October 2, 2026: Session I Courses - Last Day to Withdraw ("W" Grade) (already passed)
- Friday, November 6, 2026: Full Semester Courses – Last Day to Withdraw from Courses (“W” Grade) (already passed)
- Tuesday, November 24, 2026: Session II Courses - Last Day to Withdraw from Courses ("W" Grade)

It depends on the course session: the calendar dates above mean the standard withdrawal deadline has passed for full-semester and Session I courses, but not yet for Session II courses. A student may not withdraw after the published deadline. [6][21]

For an eligible course, after the 50% refund period you can use the online withdrawal form, complete a course withdrawal form in the Office of the Registrar, or withdraw online through Web Self Service. After the Registrar processes it, you receive a W for the course; you and the instructor of record are notified. [1] The Withdrawal Form is here: [https://www.ramapo.edu/registrar/wp-content/uploads/sites/7/2025/02/Withdrawal-Form-FILLABLE.pdf](https://www.ramapo.edu/registrar/wp-content/uploads/sites/7/2025/02/Withdrawal-Form-FILLABLE.pdf) [11] If you have a registration hold, use the Withdrawal Form or email reg@ramapo.edu from your Ramapo email with your name, Ramapo ID (R#), CRN, subject, course number, section number, and course title. [6] If you withdraw from all courses, complete the WD/LOA process in Connect using the linked instructions. [6][11]

If extraordinary circumstances prevented you from meeting the deadline, you may pursue a late administrative withdrawal. Ordinarily, apply before semester’s end; explain why you could not follow standard withdrawal procedures, identify the term, and provide supporting documentation. The Provost or designee decides whether to accept the application; a granted appeal typically results in W grades for all courses in the term. [7]

**Registrar**: Phone: (201) 684-7695. Email: reg@ramapo.edu. Office: D-224. [22]

These offices can help:
- **Center for Student Success (Academic Advising)**: Phone: (201) 684-7441. Email: success@ramapo.edu. Office: D-207. [23]
- **Counseling Center**: Phone: (201) 684-7522. Office: D-216. [23]
- **Financial Aid**: Phone: (201) 684-7549. Email: finaid@ramapo.edu. Office: E-210. [23]

Sources: [1](https://catalog.ramapo.edu/pages/R532kjMfIcfnIkM0srb3#dropping-or-withdrawing-from-a-course1) [6](https://www.ramapo.edu/registrar/withdrawing-leave-of-absence/) [7](https://www.ramapo.edu/registrar/withdrawing-leave-of-absence/) [11](https://www.ramapo.edu/registrar/forms-transcripts/) [21](https://www.ramapo.edu/academic-calendars/) [22](https://www.ramapo.edu/campus-directory/) [23](https://www.ramapo.edu/campus-directory/)

question: something fell off the ceiling in my bathroom and theres a leak. who do I call at night, public safety or facilities?

body.answer:
Sorry to hear that!

**Facilities Management**

Email: not listed on its pages [Source](https://www.ramapo.edu/facilities/). The Facilities Management pages publish no shared unit mailbox. The General Unit Contact block gives only Service Desk and Receiving / Storeroom phone numbers, work requests go through the Service Request Portal or the Service Desk phone, and the only addresses are eight named staff members' own \(excluded\).

Phones: (201) 684-7660; (201) 684-7670 (Receiving / Storeroom) [Source](https://www.ramapo.edu/facilities/)

Offices: P-FAC [Source](https://www.ramapo.edu/facilities/)

Contact note: You can submit a request using any of the following methods: Using the TMA iService Desk: Online Service Request Portal By Telephone: 201-684-7660 For Media, ITS and Telecomm requests please visit [https://helpdesk.ramapo.edu/](https://helpdesk.ramapo.edu/) If you require immediate assistance, problems such as no power, elevator malfunctions, plumbing leaks/clogs, no heat/AC any lock related problem, or health safety concerns please call the Service Desk at extension 7660. Any emergencies that occur between 4:30 p.m. and 7:30 a.m. OR on weekends should be reported to Public Safety at extension 6666. [Source](https://www.ramapo.edu/facilities/)

Hours: Monday to Friday: 7:30am-4:30pm; Saturday and Sunday: Not published. Start date: not published. End date: not published. Published note: Administrative Offices Monday - Friday, 7:30 a.m. to 4:30 p.m. [Source](https://www.ramapo.edu/facilities/)

Report an after-hours or weekend emergency: 1. Report emergencies occurring between 4:30 p.m. and 7:30 a.m., or on weekends, to Public Safety at extension 6666. \(page: “Any emergencies that occur between 4:30 p.m. and 7:30 a.m. OR on weekends should be reported to Public Safety at extension 6666.”\) [Source](https://www.ramapo.edu/facilities/service-guide/)

Get immediate assistance for an urgent Facilities problem: 1. For no power, elevator malfunctions, plumbing leaks or clogs, no heat or AC, lock problems, or health and safety concerns, call the Service Desk at extension 7660. \(page: “If you require immediate assistance, problems such as no power, elevator malfunctions, plumbing leaks/clogs, no heat/AC any lock related problem, or health safety concerns please call the Service Desk at extension 7660.”\) [Source](https://www.ramapo.edu/facilities/service-guide/)

**Public Safety \(Non-Emergency\)**

Email: publicsafety@ramapo.edu [Source](https://www.ramapo.edu/publicsafety/parking-regulations/)

Phones: (201) 684-7432; (201) 684-7789 (Director of Public Safety); (201) 684-7011 (Ramapo College Public Safety TDD) [Source](https://www.ramapo.edu/publicsafety/parking-regulations/)

Offices: C-102 [Source](https://www.ramapo.edu/publicsafety/parking-regulations/)

Contact note: If there is an imminent danger to a student, or to the community, contact the Public Safety Department at \(201\) 684-6666. Public Safety Contact Information: secdesk@ramapo.edu Parking Permits: parkingpermits@ramapo.edu [Source](https://www.ramapo.edu/publicsafety/parking-regulations/)

Hours: Monday to Sunday: 24 hours. Start date: not published. End date: not published. Published note: The Public Safety Department is available 24 hours a day, 7 days a week, 365 days a year. [Source](https://www.ramapo.edu/publicsafety/get-support/)

**Public Safety \(Emergency\)**

Phones: (201) 684-6666; (201) 684-7789 (Director of Public Safety); (201) 684-7011 (Ramapo College Public Safety TDD) [Source](https://www.ramapo.edu/publicsafety/)

**Housing & Residence Life**

Contact the right office for a facilities emergency: 1. Monday–Friday, 8:00 AM–4:30 PM: call Facilities at 201-684-7660. \(page: “Mon–Fri, 8:00 AM–4:30 PM \| The Office of Facilities \([https://www.ramapo.edu/facilities/](https://www.ramapo.edu/facilities/)\) \| 201-684-7660”\) 2. After 4:30 PM and on weekends: call Public Safety at 201-684-6666. \(page: “After 4:30 PM & Weekends \| Public Safety \| 201-684-6666”\) 3. 8:00 PM–12:00 midnight: contact the RA Hall Office. \(page: “8:00 PM–12:00 Midni… [Source](https://www.ramapo.edu/reslife/gtcl/)

question: whats my current balance and do i have any holds on my account

body.answer:
I can't see your personal records, like your grades, balance, schedule or financial aid status.

I can’t see your personal account, so I don’t have verified information about your current balance or whether you have holds. [3]

For your bill, the Student Accounts page links to the “Authorized User/Non-Current Student Login to the Bill & Payment Suite”: [https://epay.ramapo.edu/C20169_tsa/web/login.jsp](https://epay.ramapo.edu/C20169_tsa/web/login.jsp). [9] The page labels this login for authorized users and non-current students. [9]

To check registration holds, use “How Students can Check and Resolve Registration Holds” in Experience (Web Self-Service): [https://www.ramapo.edu/myadvisor/wp-content/uploads/sites/133/2026/09/How-Students-can-Check-and-Resolve-Registration-Holds-2026-1.pdf](https://www.ramapo.edu/myadvisor/wp-content/uploads/sites/133/2026/09/How-Students-can-Check-and-Resolve-Registration-Holds-2026-1.pdf). [32] Student Accounts says students with an outstanding balance who have not paid in full will have a Hold Flag; a hold may also come from another office or department. [3]

**Student Accounts**: Phone: (201) 684-7495. Email: studentaccts@ramapo.edu. Location: D-Wing, First Floor. [33]

Sources: [3](https://www.ramapo.edu/student-accounts/payment-policies/) [9](https://www.ramapo.edu/student-accounts/) [32](https://www.ramapo.edu/myadvisor/how-to-guides/) [33](https://www.ramapo.edu/campus-directory/)

question: My RA wrote me up for a candle. what happens now? do i have to go to a hearing

body.answer:
Candles are prohibited in residence halls, and Residence Life staff address violations. They may confiscate prohibited items found during inspections or when responding to alarms or incidents. [14] The pages don’t say what will happen in your specific case or whether an RA write-up automatically requires a hearing. The Office of Student Conduct is the right office to ask about your case. [1,7]

If the case concerns a fire-alarm activation due to disregard of policy, the listed first-offense outcome is a $150 fine and a Fire Safety Reflection assignment; for a second offense, a $300 fine, disciplinary probation, and possible suspension or loss of housing privileges. [2] The older Recommended Judicial Sanctions page (updated October 2022) describes the second-offense housing consequence differently—as possible Suspension of Residence Privileges. [6]

If a hearing is scheduled, you may submit documents or statements to the Office of Student Conduct before the hearing, and you may have an advisor present; the advisor cannot speak during it. You can contact the office to arrange to review or request the file used in the case. [1]

- **Housing & Residence Life**: Phone: (201) 684-7461. Email: reslife@ramapo.edu. [21]
- **Office of Student Conduct**: Phone: (201) 684-7869. Email: studentconduct@ramapo.edu. Office: C-212. [21]

question: I got a credit balance on my student account after my aid posted, how do I get that money sent to me? Do I need to sign up for direct deposit or does it just get mailed?

body.answer:

Enroll in Two-Step Verification if needed: go to Security Settings, select a passcode method, click Send Code, enter it and click Verify. In Payment Profile, edit or create a payment method and check the box in the Refund Option section to designate it for direct deposit. [3]

Student Accounts says Title IV aid credit balances of $1.00 or greater are refunded; credit balances from non-Title IV aid are subject to a $5.00 threshold. [1]

question: how do i switch roommates? we're not getting along at all

body.answer:
Roommate problems are really common, and they can be worked out. Your RA is a good first step.

Housing & Residence Life handles room changes. Review the Room Change Process webpage for step-by-step details and check the Residence Life Events & Important Dates calendar for how a change might affect you. Room changes are not guaranteed; decisions depend on available space and other factors, and professional Residence Life staff make the final decision. [1]

Submit a Room Change Request Form during the open room change period. Once housing assignments are made, Residence Life cannot accommodate requests before the semester starts. [2] The online form is linked on the Room Change Process page. [5] If approved, prorated housing charges and any applicable meal-plan changes will be adjusted on your student account; housing costs vary by building, area, and housing-unit type. Review housing and meal-plan costs through Student Accounts. [2]

Residence Life may reassign a student for unresolved conflict, among other reasons, and reserves the right to authorize or deny room and roommate changes. [4]

**Housing & Residence Life**: Phone: (201) 684-7461. Email: reslife@ramapo.edu. [21]

question: Missed 3 classes last week because I was in the hospital. How do I get my professors to excuse the absences, is there an office that sends a note or something?

body.answer:
I'm sorry you're dealing with that, and I hope you feel better soon.

Admissions’ guidance: contact your instructors to ask whether you can connect remotely and how to make up missed work; attendance is determined by the instructor. [1] If your medical condition is a disability, OSS says to contact faculty after an absence to ask if and when work may be made up; OSS can consult with you and faculty, but instructors set their attendance policies. [10]

I don’t have verified information that an office issues notes for class absences. For a medical condition, the MLOA page directs students to Student Health Services at (201) 684-7536; it does not say they provide absence notes. [2]

**Admissions**: Phone: (201) 684-7300. Email: admissions@ramapo.edu. Location: McBride House. [33]

This office can help:
**Center for Student Success (Academic Advising)**: Phone: (201) 684-7441. Email: success@ramapo.edu. Office: D-207. [34]

Sources: [1](https://www.ramapo.edu/adult-students/faqs/) [2](https://catalog.ramapo.edu/pages/R532kjMfIcfnIkM0srb3#withdrawal-or-leave-of-absence-from-the-college) [10](https://www.ramapo.edu/oss/disabilities-and-teaching-strategies-accommodations/) [33](https://www.ramapo.edu/campus-directory/) [34](https://www.ramapo.edu/campus-directory/)

question: do I get to keep my ramapo email after I graduate

body.answer:
Yes. If you have an active @ramapo.edu account, it will be migrated to an @alum.ramapo.edu account upon graduation. [6] The policy also says retired tenured faculty and retired staff with at least ten years of service may be permitted to retain a Ramapo email account upon request; that is a separate provision for retirees. [4]

Sources: [4](https://www.ramapo.edu/policies/policy/responsible-use-of-electronic-communication/) [6](https://www.ramapo.edu/alumni/)

question: how do i get a work study job on campus? i have it in my aid package but idk where to apply

body.answer:
The On-Campus Employment for Students office says to register on Handshake to view open positions, search using the keyword “RCNJ,” and follow the instructions on each posting and contact its listed supervisor. Apply to the hiring unit through Handshake. Students awarded Federal Work-Study get priority for Student Assistant positions. [5]
Federal Work-Study recipients may earn up to the award specified in their Financial Aid award letter for the academic year. [3]
The office also says students who think they might be eligible should file the FAFSA by the March 1st deadline; the Financial Aid Office notifies students if awarded Federal Work-Study. [2]

**On-Campus Employment for Students**: Phone: (201) 684-7654. Email: sap@ramapo.edu. Office: D-119. [21]

Sources: [2](https://www.ramapo.edu/on-campus-employment/faqs/) [3](https://www.ramapo.edu/on-campus-employment/) [5](https://www.ramapo.edu/on-campus-employment/) [21](https://www.ramapo.edu/campus-directory/)
